# Shared modeling helper: fiscal years run July through June.
fiscal_year_from_date <- function(date) {
  year(date) + if_else(month(date) >= 7, 1L, 0L)
}

# Raw source files are stored in the project's tables/ folder. Keep this path
# relative so the document works after cloning the project.
data_dir <- here("tables")

Executive summary

This notebook evaluates three separate PBS Utah decision-support workflows using fiscal-year rolling tests, training-only preprocessing, realistic contact capacities, and paired bootstrap uncertainty.

  • Active never-major prospects: prior-year giving is the operational benchmark; giving-history Ridge is exploratory because its modest observed improvement was not statistically reliable.
  • Current-major retention risk: giving-history Ridge is the final ranking model because it reliably outperformed the decline/recency benchmark at top-25 and top-50 capacities.
  • Former-major reactivation: prior-year giving remains the preferred transparent benchmark because Ridge did not show a reliable improvement.

Rankings are decision support, not automated outreach decisions, and should be prospectively validated with PBS outreach outcomes.

1. Data Preparation for Modeling

PBS Utah wants to identify current non-major donors who are likely to reach $1,200 or more in annual giving. The immediate outcome is conversion within 12 months; if the historical data supports it, the longer-term outcome will be conversion within 3-5 years. This analysis uses constituent, payment, legacy giving, soft-credit, campaign, Passport viewing, cultivation, and officer-portfolio data.

The purpose of this EDA is to assess data quality, coverage, and useful patterns before building a time-based prediction model. All records in this release are synthetic, so no row represents a real constituent or gift.

2. Data inventory and grain/key documentation

These datasets have different grains, including one row per constituent, payment, solicitation, or constituent-year-genre. They should not be joined at the raw-row level because doing so can duplicate records. Transactional datasets will later be aggregated to a common donor-fiscal-year grain before modeling.

File Row represents / type Unique key and links Rows / unique constituents Coverage Data-quality findings
constituents_w_memberships.csv One constituent snapshot; attribute table Constituent ID; referenced by most datasets 196,167 / 196,167 End-of-data snapshot; no dates No missing or duplicate IDs; no duplicate rows; ages are 0–120.
unite_payments.csv One payment; transaction table payment_id; donor_id → Constituent ID; marketing_code → campaign code 1,722,698 / 71,643 IDs (71,642 matched constituents + SYN-ORPHAN) FY2021–FY2026, 2020-07-01 to 2026-06-30 Content-based valid-twin checks remove 36,044 invalid-link or nonpositive copies; 1,686,654 rows remain. Synthetic labels are audit-only.
team_approach_legacy_payments.csv One legacy gift/payment; transaction table No unique transaction ID. ta_account_id is a repeating household account; constituent_id_1–_7 → Constituent ID 1,202,857 / 109,284 linked constituents 1983-07-26 to 2020-06-28, pre-FY2021 All amounts are positive. Cleaning removes 216,128 rows with no linked constituent before allocation, leaving 986,729 retained rows.
soft_credits.csv One soft credit; transaction table Credit ID; Soft Credit Constituent ID → Constituent ID 4,145 / 3,028 IDs (3,027 matched + SYN-ORPHAN) FY2021–FY2026, 2020-07-01 to 2026-06-29 Exact duplicates are removed first; valid-twin checks then remove invalid-recipient or nonpositive copies. Total removal: 192 rows; 3,953 remain.
campaign_codes.csv One marketing/campaign code; reference table Marketing Code; used by campaign members and payments 29,249 / n.a. No transaction date; includes initiative fields No missing or duplicate keys or rows. All records are marked Active and Solicitation.
campaign_members.csv One constituent solicitation/campaign-membership record; workflow/operational table No unique key. constituent_id → Constituent ID; marketing_code → Marketing Code 5,233,404 / 181,680 FY2021–FY2026; campaign markers 2020-07-01 to 2025-07-01; responses through 2026-06-30 Links are complete and valid. 56,689 exact duplicate rows; constituent/code pairs repeat in 58,786 rows, sometimes valid under the documented solicitation rules.
passport_viewing.csv One constituent × fiscal year × genre viewing record; behavioral attribute table Composite constituent_id + fiscal_year + genre; constituent ID → Constituent ID 444,741 / 70,515 FY2021–FY2026 Composite key is unique; all IDs link; no duplicate rows; viewing counts are positive and watch percentages are within 0–1.
cultivation.csv One constituent-year portfolio assignment; workflow/operational table Composite synthetic_id + fiscal_year; IDs → Constituent ID and portfolio_id → officer portfolios 4,000 / 2,398 FY2022–FY2025 Composite key is unique; all links and binary flags are valid; no duplicate rows.
officer_portfolios.csv One officer portfolio; workflow/reference table portfolio_id; referenced by cultivation 8 / n.a. Rollout FYs: 2023–2026 No missing or duplicate keys or rows.

Key implications: Payments, soft credits, campaign memberships, and Passport viewing are one-to-many relative to constituents and cannot be raw-joined without duplicating records. Campaign-member repeats are retained because they can represent valid solicitations. Content-based valid-twin checks remove copied Unite-payment and soft-credit rows, while unlinked legacy rows are removed before allocation. Individual giving uses non-organization direct payments plus soft credits, so organization-payment dollars are not double counted. Current constituent attributes are end-of-data snapshots and will need time-aware handling later to prevent leakage.

This structural check is designed to identify unexpected file sizes, schema differences, exact duplicate records, and missing-data volume before detailed quality checks begin. It does not make cleaning decisions or interpret any findings.

Missing-data checks

Missingness must be assessed by column because it can reflect unavailable information, an unknown value, or a valid absence of activity.

Code 
missing_data_summary <- imap_dfr(raw_data, function(data, file) {
  map_dfr(names(data), function(column) {
    values <- data[[column]]

    tibble(
      file_name = file,
      column_name = column,
      missing_na = sum(is.na(values)),
      percent_missing = 100 * mean(is.na(values)),
      blank_strings = if (is.character(values)) {
        sum(!is.na(values) & trimws(values) == "")
      } else {
        0L
      }
    )
  })
}) |>
  filter(missing_na > 0 | blank_strings > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(percent_missing))

Key and duplicate checks

Repeated activity is not always a duplicate: a donor can have many payments or solicitations. Duplicates must therefore be evaluated using each dataset’s documented key.

Code 
key_specs <- list(
  constituents = c("constituent_id"),
  unite_payments = c("payment_id"),
  campaign_codes = c("marketing_code"),
  passport_viewing = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year", "genre"),
  cultivation = c("synthetic_id", "fiscal_year"),
  officer_portfolios = c("portfolio_id")
)

key_quality_summary <- imap_dfr(key_specs, function(key_columns, dataset_name) {
  data <- get(dataset_name)
  missing_key <- reduce(map(key_columns, function(column) {
    values <- data[[column]]
    is.na(values) | (is.character(values) & trimws(values) == "")
  }), `|`)

  valid_keys <- data |>
    filter(!missing_key) |>
    select(all_of(key_columns))

  duplicate_key_rows <- valid_keys |>
    group_by(across(all_of(key_columns))) |>
    summarise(rows_per_key = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(rows_per_key > 1) |>
    summarise(rows_in_duplicated_keys = sum(rows_per_key)) |>
    pull(rows_in_duplicated_keys)

  tibble(
    dataset = dataset_name,
    total_rows = nrow(data),
    rows_with_missing_key = sum(missing_key),
    distinct_keys = nrow(distinct(valid_keys)),
    rows_in_duplicated_keys = replace_na(duplicate_key_rows, 0L)
  )
})

Relationship and link checks

These checks verify whether foreign keys can be linked to their documented parent tables before later aggregation. An unmatched ID does not automatically mean an error because the synthetic data includes documented SYN-ORPHAN and legacy-data exceptions.

Code 
relationship_specs <- tribble(
  ~child_dataset, ~child_key, ~parent_dataset, ~parent_key,
  "unite_payments", "donor_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "soft_credits", "soft_credit_constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "campaign_members", "constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "campaign_members", "marketing_code", "campaign_codes", "marketing_code",
  "unite_payments", "marketing_code", "campaign_codes", "marketing_code",
  "passport_viewing", "constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "cultivation", "synthetic_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "cultivation", "portfolio_id", "officer_portfolios", "portfolio_id"
)

relationship_quality_summary <- pmap_dfr(
  relationship_specs,
  function(child_dataset, child_key, parent_dataset, parent_key) {
    child_data <- get(child_dataset)
    parent_data <- get(parent_dataset)

    child_ids <- child_data |>
      transmute(foreign_key = as.character(.data[[child_key]]))
    parent_ids <- parent_data |>
      transmute(parent_key_value = as.character(.data[[parent_key]])) |>
      distinct()
    unmatched_ids <- child_ids |>
      anti_join(parent_ids, by = c("foreign_key" = "parent_key_value"))

    tibble(
      child_dataset_foreign_key = paste0(child_dataset, "$", child_key),
      parent_dataset_key = paste0(parent_dataset, "$", parent_key),
      total_child_rows = nrow(child_data),
      unmatched_child_rows = nrow(unmatched_ids),
      distinct_unmatched_ids = n_distinct(unmatched_ids$foreign_key)
    )
  }
)

Value and date-range checks

These checks identify values outside plausible ranges and describe highly skewed transaction amounts. An outlier is not automatically an error.

Code 
amount_specs <- tribble(
  ~dataset, ~column,
  "unite_payments", "payment_amount",
  "legacy_payments", "payment_amount",
  "soft_credits", "credit_amount"
)

transaction_amount_summary <- pmap_dfr(amount_specs, function(dataset, column) {
  values <- get(dataset)[[column]]
  percentiles <- quantile(
    values,
    probs = c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )

  tibble(
    amount_field = paste0(dataset, "$", column),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    zero_values = sum(values == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    negative_values = sum(values < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum = min(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    percentile_25 = percentiles[1],
    median = percentiles[2],
    percentile_75 = percentiles[3],
    percentile_95 = percentiles[4],
    maximum = max(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})

summarise_range_validity <- function(values, field, lower_bound, upper_bound) {
  tibble(
    field = field,
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    minimum = min(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    count_below_lower_bound = sum(values < lower_bound, na.rm = TRUE),
    count_above_upper_bound = sum(values > upper_bound, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

range_validity_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarise_range_validity(constituents$age, "constituents$age", 0, 120),

                           "passport_viewing$titles_viewed", 0, Inf),
  summarise_range_validity(passport_viewing$mean_percent_watched,

date_specs <- tribble(
  ~dataset, ~column,
  "unite_payments", "credit_date",
  "legacy_payments", "gift_date",
  "soft_credits", "credit_date",
  "campaign_members", "campaign_start_date",
  "campaign_members", "responded_date"
)

date_range_summary <- pmap_dfr(date_specs, function(dataset, column) {
  values <- as.Date(get(dataset)[[column]])
  nonmissing_dates <- values[!is.na(values)]

  tibble(
    date_field = paste0(dataset, "$", column),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    minimum_date = if (length(nonmissing_dates) > 0) min(nonmissing_dates) else as.Date(NA),
    maximum_date = if (length(nonmissing_dates) > 0) max(nonmissing_dates) else as.Date(NA)
  )
})

Summary of data quality findings

The raw tables contain 79 exact soft-credit duplicates and 56,689 exact campaign-member repeats. Campaign-member repeats are retained because a constituent can legitimately receive more than one solicitation. Soft-credit duplicates are removed as the first step of the completed valid-twin cleaning process. Missingness is concentrated in fields that are either unavailable in this synthetic release or structurally blank. Several University degree/employment fields, legacy descriptive and premium fields, and campaign_description are entirely missing. Campaign response_type and responded_date are missing for most records because most solicitations did not receive a response. Spouse and marital-status fields are also largely incomplete, while only two age values are missing. The constituent table is an end-of-data snapshot, so its fields will require time-aware handling later to avoid using information that would not have been available at a historical prediction date. Most foreign-key relationships are complete. The raw unmatched payment and soft-credit IDs use the documented SYN-ORPHAN placeholder, which is reported only as an audit check. Completed content-based valid-twin cleaning removes 36,044 Unite-payment copies and 192 soft-credit copies; the former includes 1,225 invalid campaign-code copies, while the latter includes 79 exact duplicates. It also removes 216,128 unlinked legacy rows before allocation. Amounts contain no negative values; nonpositive copies with valid twins are included in the verified removals, while large gifts are retained as plausible outliers. All checked dates and Passport viewing ranges were valid.

4. Cleaning decisions

The raw imported tables remain unchanged. The following rules will be applied only when creating analysis-ready copies.

Issue Decision Reason
Unite payment copies Remove only invalid donor-link, campaign-code-link, or nonpositive-amount rows when an otherwise identical valid twin exists. Content-based twin checks avoid relying on synthetic ID labels.
Soft-credit copies Remove exact duplicates first, then remove invalid-recipient or nonpositive-amount rows only when a valid twin exists. Prevents duplicate credit while retaining unmatched records that lack a valid twin.
Unlinked legacy copies Remove rows with no populated linked constituent ID before allocation. They cannot be assigned to an individual donor.
Campaign-member rows Retain all rows, including exact repeats. Repeats can be valid solicitations.
Negative amounts No action required. None were found.
Fields that are 100% missing Exclude from future feature creation. They contain no information.
Structurally missing campaign response fields Do not impute. Missing responded_date and response_type generally indicate no recorded response.
Missing Passport records Do not treat as zero viewing. Preserve missingness and coverage as a separate concept.
Missing age and other partially missing constituent fields Retain as missing for now. Any model imputation must later be fit using training data only.
End-of-data constituent snapshot fields Do not use directly as historical predictors unless a time-valid version can be created. They could introduce data leakage.
Unite payments with an unmatched marketing code Retain the payment for giving totals; treat campaign information as unknown unless the code can be mapped later. The payment remains valid for giving analysis.
Large gifts Retain. They are plausible donor behavior, not demonstrated errors.

The next subsection applies these rules to create analysis-ready copies while preserving the raw tables.

Creating analysis-ready copies

The following code creates new analysis-ready objects while preserving all raw objects for audit. These copies apply only the documented record-level rules; they do not aggregate transactions, impute values, or create modeling features.

Code 
content_twin_key <- function(data, columns) {
  do.call(
    paste,
    c(
      lapply(data[columns], function(value) replace_na(as.character(value), "<NA>")),
      sep = "\u001f"
    )
  )
}

valid_constituent_ids <- as.character(constituents$constituent_id)
valid_campaign_codes <- as.character(campaign_codes$marketing_code)

# A valid twin matches every substantive field except the record ID and the
# field that makes the candidate invalid. Synthetic labels are audit-only.
unite_payment_columns <- names(unite_payments)
unite_payment_candidates <- unite_payments |>
  mutate(
    valid_donor_link = donor_id %in% valid_constituent_ids,
    valid_campaign_link = marketing_code %in% valid_campaign_codes,
    valid_amount = coalesce(payment_amount > 0, FALSE)
  )

unite_donor_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "donor_id"))
)
unite_campaign_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "marketing_code"))
)
unite_amount_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "payment_amount"))
)

unite_payments_flagged <- unite_payment_candidates |>
  mutate(
    invalid_donor_copy = !valid_donor_link &
      unite_donor_twin_key %in% unite_donor_twin_key[valid_donor_link],
    invalid_campaign_copy = !valid_campaign_link &
      unite_campaign_twin_key %in% unite_campaign_twin_key[valid_campaign_link],
    nonpositive_amount_copy = !valid_amount &
      unite_amount_twin_key %in% unite_amount_twin_key[valid_amount],
    remove_valid_twin_copy = invalid_donor_copy | invalid_campaign_copy |
      nonpositive_amount_copy
  )

unite_payments_analysis <- unite_payments_flagged |>
  filter(!remove_valid_twin_copy) |>
  mutate(
    positive_amount = valid_amount,
    campaign_code_matched = valid_campaign_link
  )

soft_credit_exact_duplicate <- duplicated(soft_credits)
soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication <- soft_credits |>
  filter(!soft_credit_exact_duplicate)
soft_credit_columns <- names(soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication)
soft_credit_candidates <- soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication |>
  mutate(
    valid_recipient_link = soft_credit_constituent_id %in% valid_constituent_ids,
    valid_amount = coalesce(credit_amount > 0, FALSE)
  )

soft_recipient_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  soft_credit_candidates,
  setdiff(soft_credit_columns, c("credit_id", "soft_credit_constituent_id"))
)
soft_amount_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  soft_credit_candidates,
  setdiff(soft_credit_columns, c("credit_id", "credit_amount"))
)

soft_credits_flagged <- soft_credit_candidates |>
  mutate(
    invalid_recipient_copy = !valid_recipient_link &
      soft_recipient_twin_key %in% soft_recipient_twin_key[valid_recipient_link],
    nonpositive_amount_copy = !valid_amount &
      soft_amount_twin_key %in% soft_amount_twin_key[valid_amount],
    remove_valid_twin_copy = invalid_recipient_copy | nonpositive_amount_copy,
    positive_amount = valid_amount
  )

soft_credits_analysis <- soft_credits_flagged |>
  filter(!remove_valid_twin_copy)

legacy_id_columns <- paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7)
legacy_payment_candidates <- legacy_payments |>
  mutate(
    has_linked_constituent = if_any(
      all_of(legacy_id_columns),
      ~ !is.na(.x) & trimws(as.character(.x)) != ""
    ),
    remove_unlinked_copy = !has_linked_constituent
  )
legacy_payments_analysis <- legacy_payment_candidates |>
  filter(!remove_unlinked_copy)

campaign_members_analysis <- campaign_members

organization_constituents <- constituents |>
  filter(
    primary_constituent_type == "Organization" |
      str_detect(
        coalesce(as.character(constituent_type), ""),
        regex("Organization", ignore_case = TRUE)
      )
  ) |>
  select(constituent_id, primary_constituent_type, constituent_type)

unite_payments_analysis <- unite_payments_analysis |>
  mutate(organization_payment = donor_id %in% organization_constituents$constituent_id)

constituents_analysis <- constituents

cultivation_analysis <- cultivation
officer_portfolios_analysis <- officer_portfolios

5. Data Preparation for Modeling

6. Building the donor–fiscal-year dataset

Annual giving base

The model needs one record per constituent per fiscal year. Individual annual giving equals positive non-organization direct payments plus positive soft credits. Legacy payments are handled separately because they are household- level and predate FY2021.

Code 
positive_individual_unite_payments <- unite_payments_analysis |>
  filter(!organization_payment, positive_amount) |>
  mutate(fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_from_date(credit_date)))

excluded_organization_payments <- unite_payments_analysis |>
  filter(organization_payment, positive_amount) |>
  mutate(fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_from_date(credit_date)))

positive_soft_credits <- soft_credits_analysis |>
  filter(positive_amount) |>
  mutate(fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_from_date(credit_date)))

direct_payment_transactions <- positive_individual_unite_payments |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id = as.character(donor_id),
    fiscal_year,
    gift_credit_date = credit_date,
    amount = payment_amount,
    source = "direct_payment"
  )

soft_credit_transactions <- positive_soft_credits |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id = as.character(soft_credit_constituent_id),
    fiscal_year,
    gift_credit_date = credit_date,
    amount = credit_amount,
    source = "soft_credit"
  )

constituent_giving_transactions <- bind_rows(
  direct_payment_transactions,
  soft_credit_transactions
)

donor_fiscal_year_giving <- constituent_giving_transactions |>
  group_by(constituent_id, fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    annual_giving = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    direct_payment_dollars = sum(amount[source == "direct_payment"], na.rm = TRUE),
    soft_credit_dollars = sum(amount[source == "soft_credit"], na.rm = TRUE),
    direct_payment_count = sum(source == "direct_payment"),
    soft_credit_count = sum(source == "soft_credit"),
    largest_gift = max(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    first_gift_date = min(gift_credit_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_gift_date = max(gift_credit_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

Individual direct payments and soft credits are retained as separate credit sources; organization payments are excluded before individual-level giving is constructed and audited against soft-credit dollars by fiscal year. designation_detail_id is not used as a transaction-level deduplication key because it can occur on many payment records. This analysis does not attempt to calculate station revenue by summing the two sources. Organization records are already identified, and their direct payments are excluded from individual- level giving.

Eligible donor-year panel and major-donor status

An eligible donor is a constituent with at least one positive, linked PBS Utah giving record during the available FY2021–FY2026 period. The model will later exclude donors who are already major donors at the prediction date. This definition should be confirmed with PBS Utah before deployment.

Code 
eligible_donors <- donor_fiscal_year_giving |>
  distinct(constituent_id)

observed_fiscal_year_bounds <- donor_fiscal_year_giving |>
  transmute(fiscal_year_number = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(fiscal_year, "FY"))) |>
  summarise(
    first_fiscal_year = min(fiscal_year_number),
    last_fiscal_year = max(fiscal_year_number)
  )

observed_fiscal_years <- paste0(
  "FY",
  seq(observed_fiscal_year_bounds$first_fiscal_year,
      observed_fiscal_year_bounds$last_fiscal_year)
)

donor_fiscal_year_panel <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  constituent_id = eligible_donors$constituent_id,
  fiscal_year = observed_fiscal_years
) |>
  left_join(donor_fiscal_year_giving, by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")) |>
  mutate(
    annual_giving = replace_na(annual_giving, 0),
    direct_payment_dollars = replace_na(direct_payment_dollars, 0),
    soft_credit_dollars = replace_na(soft_credit_dollars, 0),
    direct_payment_count = replace_na(direct_payment_count, 0L),
    soft_credit_count = replace_na(soft_credit_count, 0L),
    largest_gift = replace_na(largest_gift, 0),
    gave_this_year = annual_giving > 0,
    is_major_donor = annual_giving >= 1200,
    giving_tier = case_when(
      annual_giving == 0 ~ "No giving",
      annual_giving < 1200 ~ "Under $1,200",
      annual_giving < 2000 ~ "$1,200–$1,999",
      annual_giving < 5000 ~ "$2,000–$4,999",
      annual_giving < 10000 ~ "$5,000–$9,999",
      annual_giving < 15000 ~ "$10,000–$14,999",
      TRUE ~ "$15,000+"
    ),
    giving_tier = factor(
      giving_tier,
      levels = c(
        "No giving", "Under $1,200", "$1,200–$1,999", "$2,000–$4,999",
        "$5,000–$9,999", "$10,000–$14,999", "$15,000+"
      )
    )
  )

donor_fiscal_year_summary <- donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    eligible_donors = n_distinct(constituent_id),
    donors_who_gave = sum(gave_this_year),
    major_donors = sum(is_major_donor),
    major_donor_percentage = major_donors / eligible_donors,
    total_annual_giving = sum(annual_giving, na.rm = TRUE),
    major_donor_annual_giving = sum(annual_giving[is_major_donor], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year)

Individual versus organization eligibility check

The constituent table may contain both people and organizations. Because this project is intended to rank individual major-donor prospects, entity type must be understood before finalizing the eligible population.

Code 
constituent_type_frequency <- bind_rows(
  constituents_analysis |>
    filter(!is.na(primary_constituent_type),
           trimws(primary_constituent_type) != "") |>
    count(primary_constituent_type, name = "constituents") |>
    mutate(type_field = "primary_constituent_type",
           type_value = primary_constituent_type) |>
    select(type_field, type_value, constituents),
  constituents_analysis |>
    filter(!is.na(constituent_type), trimws(constituent_type) != "") |>
    count(constituent_type, name = "constituents") |>
    mutate(type_field = "constituent_type", type_value = constituent_type) |>
    select(type_field, type_value, constituents)
) |>
  arrange(type_field, desc(constituents))

organization_pattern <- regex(
  "organization|foundation|business|corporation|trust|estate",
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

potential_organization_records <- constituents_analysis |>
  mutate(
    primary_constituent_type = as.character(primary_constituent_type),
    constituent_type = as.character(constituent_type)

  filter(
    str_detect(coalesce(primary_constituent_type, ""), organization_pattern) |

Time-aware eligible donor panel

A donor can enter the historical modeling population only after their first positive, linked PBS Utah gift. Including a person before that first gift would use future information and create data leakage.

Code 
first_giving_year <- donor_fiscal_year_giving |>
  filter(annual_giving > 0) |>
  mutate(fiscal_year_number = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(fiscal_year, "FY"))) |>
  group_by(constituent_id) |>
  summarise(first_giving_year = min(fiscal_year_number), .groups = "drop")

modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel <- donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  filter(!constituent_id %in% organization_constituents$constituent_id) |>
  mutate(fiscal_year_number = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(fiscal_year, "FY"))) |>
  left_join(first_giving_year, by = "constituent_id") |>
  filter(fiscal_year_number >= first_giving_year) |>
  select(-fiscal_year_number)

time_aware_individual_panel_summary <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    eligible_donors = n_distinct(constituent_id),
    donors_who_gave = sum(gave_this_year),
    major_donors = sum(is_major_donor),
    major_donor_percentage = major_donors / eligible_donors,
    total_annual_giving = sum(annual_giving, na.rm = TRUE),
    major_donor_annual_giving = sum(annual_giving[is_major_donor], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year)

      across(c(total_annual_giving, major_donor_annual_giving), scales::dollar)
    ),
  format = "pipe"
)

Legacy giving linkage check

Legacy payments are household-level and can link to up to seven constituents. Before using them for historical donor eligibility or features, the analysis must determine how often a gift links to one person versus multiple people.

Code 
legacy_id_columns <- paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7)

legacy_link_matrix <- legacy_payments_analysis |>
  select(all_of(legacy_id_columns)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) |>
  as.matrix()

legacy_link_present <- !is.na(legacy_link_matrix) &
  trimws(legacy_link_matrix) != ""
legacy_link_count <- rowSums(legacy_link_present)

legacy_linkage_summary <- tibble(
  linkage_group = case_when(
    legacy_link_count == 0 ~ "Zero linked constituents",
    legacy_link_count == 1 ~ "Exactly one linked constituent",
    legacy_link_count == 2 ~ "Two linked constituents",
    legacy_link_count >= 3 ~ "Three or more linked constituents"
  )
) |>
  count(linkage_group, name = "legacy_rows") |>
  mutate(percentage = legacy_rows / sum(legacy_rows)) |>
  arrange(factor(
    linkage_group,
    levels = c(
      "Zero linked constituents", "Exactly one linked constituent",
      "Two linked constituents", "Three or more linked constituents"
    )
  ))

legacy_position_summary <- tibble(
  linked_id_position = colnames(legacy_link_matrix),
  populated_rows = colSums(legacy_link_present),
  percentage_of_legacy_rows = populated_rows / nrow(legacy_link_matrix)
)

legacy_link_ids <- legacy_link_matrix[legacy_link_present]
constituent_ids <- as.character(constituents_analysis$constituent_id)
legacy_link_match_summary <- tibble(
  nonmissing_legacy_constituent_ids = length(legacy_link_ids),
  unmatched_legacy_constituent_ids = sum(!legacy_link_ids %in% constituent_ids),
  all_nonmissing_ids_match = all(legacy_link_ids %in% constituent_ids)
)

two_person_linkage_patterns <- tibble(
  linked_constituent_count = legacy_link_count,
  linkage_pattern = apply(
    legacy_link_present,
    1,
    function(position_present) {
      paste(colnames(legacy_link_matrix)[position_present], collapse = " + ")
    }
  )
) |>
  filter(linked_constituent_count == 2) |>
  count(linkage_pattern, name = "legacy_rows") |>
  arrange(desc(legacy_rows))

The next step will document an allocation rule for usable legacy history.

Legacy history allocation rule

The retained legacy rows are household-level. For individual-level historical context, each retained record is assigned only to its primary constituent_id_1. When a secondary linked constituent exists, the record is flagged but still assigned only to the primary ID to avoid double counting; this is a documented limitation.

Code 
legacy_individual_history <- legacy_payments_analysis |>
  filter(!is.na(constituent_id_1), trimws(as.character(constituent_id_1)) != "") |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id = as.character(constituent_id_1),
    legacy_fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_from_date(gift_date)),
    gift_date,
    payment_amount,
    multiple_linked_constituents = !is.na(constituent_id_2) &
      trimws(as.character(constituent_id_2)) != ""
  )

legacy_no_linked_constituent_rows <- sum(legacy_link_count == 0)

legacy_history_audit <- tibble(
  metric = c(
    "Total legacy rows",
    "Rows excluded because no constituent is linked",
    "Rows assigned to a primary constituent",
    "Rows with multiple linked constituents",
    "Total legacy dollars assigned to primary constituent history"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(legacy_payments_analysis),
    legacy_no_linked_constituent_rows,
    nrow(legacy_individual_history),
    sum(legacy_individual_history$multiple_linked_constituents),
    sum(legacy_individual_history$payment_amount, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

legacy_donor_summary <- legacy_individual_history |>
  group_by(constituent_id) |>
  summarise(
    first_legacy_gift_date = min(gift_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_legacy_gift_date = max(gift_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    lifetime_legacy_giving = sum(payment_amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    legacy_gift_count = n(),
    multiple_linked_constituents = any(multiple_linked_constituents),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(

    mutate(value = if_else(
      metric == "Total legacy dollars assigned to primary constituent history",
      scales::dollar(value),

Final time-aware individual donor panel

Eligibility now uses the earliest linked gift in either legacy history or FY2021–FY2026 giving history. A donor is eligible in a fiscal year only if their first known linked gift occurred on or before that fiscal year’s June 30 end date.

Code 
combined_donor_history <- bind_rows(
  legacy_individual_history |>
    transmute(constituent_id, gift_date, history_source = "legacy"),
  constituent_giving_transactions |>
    transmute(
      constituent_id,
      gift_date = gift_credit_date,
      history_source = source
    )
)

first_known_gift <- combined_donor_history |>
  group_by(constituent_id) |>
  summarise(first_known_gift_date = min(gift_date, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

modeling_fiscal_years <- donor_fiscal_year_giving |>
  distinct(fiscal_year) |>
  mutate(
    fiscal_year_number = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(fiscal_year, "FY")),
    fiscal_year_end_date = as.Date(paste0(fiscal_year_number, "-06-30"))
  ) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year)

modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  constituent_id = setdiff(
    first_known_gift$constituent_id,
    organization_constituents$constituent_id
  ),
  modeling_fiscal_years
) |>
  left_join(first_known_gift, by = "constituent_id") |>
  filter(first_known_gift_date <= fiscal_year_end_date) |>
  left_join(donor_fiscal_year_giving, by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")) |>
  mutate(
    annual_giving = replace_na(annual_giving, 0),
    direct_payment_dollars = replace_na(direct_payment_dollars, 0),
    soft_credit_dollars = replace_na(soft_credit_dollars, 0),
    direct_payment_count = replace_na(direct_payment_count, 0L),
    soft_credit_count = replace_na(soft_credit_count, 0L),
    largest_gift = replace_na(largest_gift, 0),
    gave_this_year = annual_giving > 0,
    is_major_donor = annual_giving >= 1200,
    giving_tier = case_when(
      annual_giving == 0 ~ "No giving",
      annual_giving < 1200 ~ "Under $1,200",
      annual_giving < 2000 ~ "$1,200–$1,999",
      annual_giving < 5000 ~ "$2,000–$4,999",
      annual_giving < 10000 ~ "$5,000–$9,999",
      annual_giving < 15000 ~ "$10,000–$14,999",
      TRUE ~ "$15,000+"
    ),
    giving_tier = factor(
      giving_tier,
      levels = c(
        "No giving", "Under $1,200", "$1,200–$1,999", "$2,000–$4,999",
        "$5,000–$9,999", "$10,000–$14,999", "$15,000+"
      )
    )
  )

Code 
# Household status uses only reciprocal spouse links between known individual
# constituents. Unsupported links remain one-person households; the source has
# no relationship-effective dates, so supported links are a documented proxy.
individual_constituents <- constituents_analysis |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id = as.character(constituent_id),
    spouse_constituent_id = na_if(trimws(as.character(spouse_constituent_id)), ""),
    is_individual = !(
      primary_constituent_type == "Organization" |
        str_detect(coalesce(as.character(constituent_type), ""),
                   regex("Organization", ignore_case = TRUE))
    )
  ) |>
  filter(is_individual) |>
  select(-is_individual)

spouse_link_check <- individual_constituents |>
  filter(!is.na(spouse_constituent_id)) |>
  left_join(
    individual_constituents |>
      transmute(
        spouse_constituent_id = constituent_id,
        spouse_points_back = spouse_constituent_id
      ),
    by = "spouse_constituent_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    supported_reciprocal_link =
      !is.na(spouse_points_back) & spouse_points_back == constituent_id,
    self_link = spouse_constituent_id == constituent_id
  )

household_map <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  distinct(constituent_id) |>
  mutate(constituent_id = as.character(constituent_id)) |>
  left_join(
    spouse_link_check |>
      select(constituent_id, spouse_constituent_id, supported_reciprocal_link),
    by = "constituent_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    supported_reciprocal_link = replace_na(supported_reciprocal_link, FALSE),
    household_id = if_else(
      supported_reciprocal_link,
      pmin(constituent_id, spouse_constituent_id),
      constituent_id
    )
  ) |>
  select(constituent_id, household_id, supported_reciprocal_link)

household_link_audit <- tibble(
  metric = c(
    "Constituents with a populated spouse link",
    "Supported reciprocal spouse-link rows",
    "Unsupported or nonreciprocal spouse-link rows",
    "Self-referential spouse-link rows"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(spouse_link_check),
    sum(spouse_link_check$supported_reciprocal_link),
    sum(!spouse_link_check$supported_reciprocal_link),
    sum(spouse_link_check$self_link)
  )
)

household_fiscal_year_giving <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  mutate(constituent_id = as.character(constituent_id)) |>
  left_join(household_map, by = "constituent_id") |>
  group_by(household_id, fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(household_annual_giving = sum(annual_giving), .groups = "drop")

# Retained legacy records stay allocated to constituent_id_1. They provide
# pre-FY2021 major-history evidence without inferring unsupported households.
legacy_household_major_history <- legacy_individual_history |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id = as.character(constituent_id),
    legacy_fiscal_year,
    payment_amount
  ) |>
  inner_join(household_map, by = "constituent_id") |>
  group_by(household_id, legacy_fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(legacy_household_annual_giving = sum(payment_amount), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(legacy_household_annual_giving >= 1200) |>
  distinct(household_id) |>
  mutate(has_legacy_major_history = TRUE)

modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  mutate(constituent_id = as.character(constituent_id)) |>
  left_join(household_map, by = "constituent_id") |>
  left_join(household_fiscal_year_giving, by = c("household_id", "fiscal_year")) |>
  left_join(legacy_household_major_history, by = "household_id") |>
  mutate(
    household_annual_giving = replace_na(household_annual_giving, 0),
    is_household_major_donor = household_annual_giving >= 1200,
    has_legacy_major_history = replace_na(has_legacy_major_history, FALSE)
  ) |>
  arrange(constituent_id, fiscal_year) |>
  group_by(constituent_id) |>
  mutate(
    prior_current_major_history = lag(cumany(is_household_major_donor),
                                      default = FALSE),
    former_major = has_legacy_major_history | prior_current_major_history,
    gave_in_prior_1y = lag(gave_this_year, 1, default = FALSE),
    gave_in_prior_2y = lag(gave_this_year, 2, default = FALSE),
    cohort_group = case_when(
      gave_this_year & !is_household_major_donor & !former_major ~
        "Primary active never-major",
      gave_this_year & !is_household_major_donor & former_major ~
        "Former-major reactivation",
      !gave_this_year & !is_household_major_donor &
        (gave_in_prior_1y | gave_in_prior_2y) ~ "Lapsed",
      is_household_major_donor ~ "Current household major",
      TRUE ~ "Other inactive"
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

    )
  ) |>
  count(history_group, name = "donors")

7. Target-variable EDA

Twelve-month major-donor conversion

At the end of each fiscal year, the primary model cohort contains active individual donors who are not currently household-major and have no prior major history in the retained legacy or earlier fiscal-year record. Former-major donors are reported separately as a reactivation cohort and are not included in the primary model. Lapsed donors are also reported separately and are not included in modeling.

Code 
snapshot_years <- paste0("FY", 2021:2025)

following_year_outcomes <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  mutate(
    fiscal_year_number = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(fiscal_year, "FY")),
    snapshot_fiscal_year = paste0("FY", fiscal_year_number - 1)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id,
    snapshot_fiscal_year,
    following_year_annual_giving = annual_giving,
    following_year_is_major_donor = is_household_major_donor
  )

primary_conversion_12m_panel <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  filter(
    fiscal_year %in% snapshot_years,
    cohort_group == "Primary active never-major"
  ) |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id,
    snapshot_fiscal_year = fiscal_year,
    snapshot_annual_giving = annual_giving
  ) |>
  left_join(
    following_year_outcomes,
    by = c("constituent_id", "snapshot_fiscal_year")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    converts_to_major_next_fy = following_year_is_major_donor
  )

reactivation_conversion_12m_panel <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  filter(
    fiscal_year %in% snapshot_years,
    cohort_group == "Former-major reactivation"
  ) |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id,
    snapshot_fiscal_year = fiscal_year,
    snapshot_annual_giving = annual_giving
  ) |>
  left_join(following_year_outcomes,
            by = c("constituent_id", "snapshot_fiscal_year")) |>
  mutate(converts_to_major_next_fy = following_year_is_major_donor)

lapsed_12m_panel <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  filter(fiscal_year %in% snapshot_years, cohort_group == "Lapsed") |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id,

    snapshot_annual_giving = annual_giving
  ) |>
  left_join(following_year_outcomes,
            by = c("constituent_id", "snapshot_fiscal_year")) |>
  mutate(converts_to_major_next_fy = following_year_is_major_donor)

Twelve-month conversion is a rare outcome, so majority-class accuracy is not a useful measure of prospect-ranking quality.

Three- and five-year major-donor conversion

A donor is a longer-term converter if they are not a major donor at the snapshot date but reach at least $1,200 in annual giving in any future fiscal year within the stated horizon. Complete 3-year follow-up is available for FY2021–FY2023, while complete 5-year follow-up is available only for FY2021. Therefore, the 3-year target can be explored across multiple years, but the 5-year result is descriptive rather than a robust model-validation sample.

Code 
modeling_panel_with_year_number <- modeling_donor_fiscal_year_panel |>
  mutate(fiscal_year_number = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(fiscal_year, "FY")))

conversion_3y_panel <- modeling_panel_with_year_number |>
  filter(fiscal_year_number %in% 2021:2023, !is_major_donor) |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id,
    snapshot_fiscal_year = fiscal_year,
    snapshot_year_number = fiscal_year_number
  ) |>
  left_join(
    modeling_panel_with_year_number |>
      transmute(
        constituent_id,
        future_year_number = fiscal_year_number,
        future_annual_giving = annual_giving
      ),
    by = "constituent_id",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  filter(
    future_year_number > snapshot_year_number,
    future_year_number <= snapshot_year_number + 3
  ) |>
  group_by(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, snapshot_year_number) |>
  summarise(
    converts_to_major_within_3y = any(future_annual_giving >= 1200),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

conversion_3y_summary <- conversion_3y_panel |>
  group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    eligible_non_major_donors = n(),
    three_year_converters = sum(converts_to_major_within_3y),
    conversion_rate = mean(converts_to_major_within_3y),
    majority_class_baseline_accuracy = 1 - conversion_rate,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(snapshot_fiscal_year)

conversion_3y_overall_summary <- conversion_3y_panel |>
  summarise(
    eligible_non_major_donors = n(),
    three_year_converters = sum(converts_to_major_within_3y),

Giving-history features

Every predictor must use information available on or before the snapshot fiscal-year end date. Future giving must never be used to predict conversion. These features use only individual-level legacy and current giving transactions dated by each donor-year snapshot.

Code 
# Build RFM features efficiently from donor × fiscal-year summaries.
# All snapshots occur at the end of a PBS Utah fiscal year (June 30).

candidate_base <- conversion_12m_panel |>
  mutate(
    snapshot_year_number = as.integer(str_remove(snapshot_fiscal_year, "FY")),
    snapshot_end_date = as.Date(paste0(snapshot_year_number, "-06-30"))
  )

candidate_ids <- candidate_base |>
  distinct(constituent_id)

giving_history_transactions <- bind_rows(
  legacy_individual_history |>
    transmute(
      constituent_id,
      gift_date,
      amount = payment_amount,
      gift_fiscal_year = legacy_fiscal_year,
      source = "legacy"
    ),
  constituent_giving_transactions |>
    transmute(
      constituent_id,
      gift_date = gift_credit_date,
      amount,
      gift_fiscal_year = fiscal_year,
      source
    )
)

# Aggregate raw gift history once, rather than once for every donor-year row.
history_by_fiscal_year <- giving_history_transactions |>
  semi_join(candidate_ids, by = "constituent_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(gift_date), !is.na(amount)) |>
  mutate(
    gift_fiscal_year_number = as.integer(
      str_remove(gift_fiscal_year, "FY")
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(constituent_id, gift_fiscal_year_number) |>
  summarise(
    fiscal_year_giving = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    fiscal_year_gift_count = n(),
    fiscal_year_largest_gift = max(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    first_gift_date_in_fy = min(gift_date),
    last_gift_date_in_fy = max(gift_date),
    legacy_giving_in_fy = any(source == "legacy"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Build one feature table per snapshot year, then combine them.
rfm_runtime <- system.time({

  rfm_predictor_eda <- map_dfr(
    sort(unique(candidate_base$snapshot_year_number)),
    function(snapshot_year_number) {

      snapshot_candidates <- candidate_base |>
        filter(snapshot_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number)

      # This table is already aggregated to donor × fiscal year.
      # It is much smaller than raw transaction history.
      history_to_snapshot <- history_by_fiscal_year |>
        filter(gift_fiscal_year_number <= .env$snapshot_year_number) |>
        group_by(constituent_id) |>
        summarise(
          giving_last_12m = sum(
            fiscal_year_giving[
              gift_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          giving_last_36m = sum(
            fiscal_year_giving[
              gift_fiscal_year_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 2
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          giving_previous_two_years = sum(
            fiscal_year_giving[
              gift_fiscal_year_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 2 &
                gift_fiscal_year_number <= .env$snapshot_year_number - 1
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          years_given_last_5 = n_distinct(
            gift_fiscal_year_number[
              gift_fiscal_year_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 4 &
                gift_fiscal_year_number <= .env$snapshot_year_number
            ]
          ),
          giving_previous_12m = sum(
            fiscal_year_giving[
              gift_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number - 1
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          gift_count_last_12m = sum(
            fiscal_year_gift_count[
              gift_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          lifetime_giving_to_date = sum(fiscal_year_giving, na.rm = TRUE),
          lifetime_gift_count = sum(fiscal_year_gift_count, na.rm = TRUE),
          largest_prior_gift = max(fiscal_year_largest_gift, na.rm = TRUE),
          first_known_gift_date = min(first_gift_date_in_fy),
          last_known_gift_date = max(last_gift_date_in_fy),
          had_legacy_giving_history = any(legacy_giving_in_fy),
          gave_in_snapshot_year = any(
            gift_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
          ),
          .groups = "drop"
        )

      snapshot_candidates |>
        left_join(history_to_snapshot, by = "constituent_id") |>
        mutate(
          giving_last_12m = replace_na(giving_last_12m, 0),
          giving_last_36m = replace_na(giving_last_36m, 0),
          giving_previous_two_years = replace_na(giving_previous_two_years, 0),
          years_given_last_5 = replace_na(years_given_last_5, 0L),
          giving_previous_12m = replace_na(giving_previous_12m, 0),
          gift_count_last_12m = replace_na(gift_count_last_12m, 0L),
          lifetime_giving_to_date = replace_na(lifetime_giving_to_date, 0),
          lifetime_gift_count = replace_na(lifetime_gift_count, 0L),
          largest_prior_gift = replace_na(largest_prior_gift, 0),
          gave_in_snapshot_year = replace_na(gave_in_snapshot_year, FALSE),
          had_legacy_giving_history = replace_na(
            had_legacy_giving_history, FALSE
          ),
          months_since_last_gift = if_else(
            !is.na(last_known_gift_date),
            interval(last_known_gift_date, snapshot_end_date) %/% months(1),
            NA_integer_
          ),
          days_since_last_gift = if_else(
            !is.na(last_known_gift_date),
            as.integer(snapshot_end_date - last_known_gift_date),
            NA_integer_
          ),
          donor_tenure_years = if_else(
            !is.na(first_known_gift_date),
            time_length(
              interval(first_known_gift_date, snapshot_end_date),
              "years"
            ),
            NA_real_
          )
        ) |>
        select(-first_known_gift_date, -last_known_gift_date) |>
        mutate(giving_change_from_last_year =
          giving_last_12m - giving_previous_12m)
    }
  )
})

Prior-year-giving ranking benchmark

Before fitting a model, prior-year giving is used as a transparent ranking benchmark. Each fiscal-year test cohort is ranked independently by giving_last_12m; the pooled row combines the three fiscal-year top-1,000 lists, preserving the same contact capacity within each cohort.

Code 
rank_giving_benchmark <- function(data, cohort_label) {
  ranked <- data |>
    arrange(desc(giving_last_12m), constituent_id) |>
    mutate(rank_by_prior_year_giving = row_number())

  selected <- ranked |>
    filter(rank_by_prior_year_giving <= min(1000L, nrow(ranked)))

  tibble(
    test_cohort = cohort_label,
    donor_years = nrow(ranked),
    converters = sum(ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    contact_capacity = nrow(selected),
    recall_at_1000 = if_else(
      sum(ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy) > 0,
      sum(selected$converts_to_major_next_fy) /
        sum(ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy),
      NA_real_
    ),
    precision_at_1000 = mean(selected$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    lift_at_1000 = precision_at_1000 /
      mean(ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy)
  )
}

benchmark_test_cohorts <- rfm_predictor_eda |>
  filter(snapshot_fiscal_year %in% paste0("FY", 2022:2024))

prior_year_giving_benchmark_by_cohort <- benchmark_test_cohorts |>
  group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
  group_modify(~ rank_giving_benchmark(.x, .y$snapshot_fiscal_year)) |>
  ungroup()

prior_year_giving_benchmark_pooled <- benchmark_test_cohorts |>
  group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
  group_modify(~ {
    ranked <- .x |>
      arrange(desc(giving_last_12m), constituent_id) |>
      mutate(rank_by_prior_year_giving = row_number())
    filter(ranked, rank_by_prior_year_giving <= min(1000L, nrow(ranked)))
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  summarise(
    test_cohort = "Pooled (top 1,000 per FY)",
    donor_years = nrow(benchmark_test_cohorts),
    converters = sum(benchmark_test_cohorts$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    contact_capacity = n(),
    recall_at_1000 = sum(converts_to_major_next_fy) /
      sum(benchmark_test_cohorts$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    precision_at_1000 = mean(converts_to_major_next_fy),
    lift_at_1000 = precision_at_1000 /
      mean(benchmark_test_cohorts$converts_to_major_next_fy)
  )

Rolling ridge logistic-regression benchmark

The ridge model is evaluated only in the primary active never-major cohort. It uses pre-specified giving-history features, with all imputation, transformation parameters, scaling, and penalty tuning learned separately in each training window. No resampling, campaign, Passport, cultivation, officer, cohort-status, or constituent-snapshot fields are included.

Code 
ridge_feature_names <- c(
  "giving_last_12m",
  "giving_previous_two_years",
  "years_given_last_5",
  "years_since_first_gift",
  "giving_change_from_last_year",
  "largest_prior_gift",
  "days_since_last_gift",
  "had_legacy_giving_history"
)

ridge_model_data <- rfm_predictor_eda |>
  transmute(
    constituent_id,
    snapshot_fiscal_year,
    converts_to_major_next_fy,
    giving_last_12m,
    giving_previous_two_years,
    years_given_last_5,
    years_since_first_gift = donor_tenure_years,
    giving_change_from_last_year,
    largest_prior_gift,
    days_since_last_gift,
    had_legacy_giving_history = as.numeric(had_legacy_giving_history)
  )

impute_and_transform_ridge_features <- function(data, training_medians) {
  features <- data |>
    select(all_of(ridge_feature_names)) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

  for (feature_name in ridge_feature_names) {
    features[[feature_name]][is.na(features[[feature_name]])] <-
      training_medians[[feature_name]]
  }

  features |>
    mutate(
      giving_last_12m = log1p(giving_last_12m),
      giving_previous_two_years = log1p(giving_previous_two_years),
      years_since_first_gift = log1p(years_since_first_gift),
      giving_change_from_last_year = sign(giving_change_from_last_year) *
        log1p(abs(giving_change_from_last_year)),
      largest_prior_gift = log1p(largest_prior_gift),
      days_since_last_gift = log1p(days_since_last_gift)
    ) |>
    as.matrix()
}

fit_ridge_preprocessor <- function(training_data) {
  raw_features <- training_data |>
    select(all_of(ridge_feature_names)) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

  training_medians <- vapply(
    raw_features,
    function(value) {
      median_value <- median(value, na.rm = TRUE)
      if_else(is.na(median_value), 0, median_value)
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  transformed_training <- impute_and_transform_ridge_features(
    training_data,
    training_medians
  )
  training_means <- colMeans(transformed_training)
  training_sds <- apply(transformed_training, 2, sd)
  training_sds[is.na(training_sds) | training_sds == 0] <- 1

  list(
    medians = training_medians,
    means = training_means,
    sds = training_sds
  )
}

apply_ridge_preprocessor <- function(data, preprocessor) {
  transformed <- impute_and_transform_ridge_features(data, preprocessor$medians)
  sweep(
    sweep(transformed, 2, preprocessor$means, "-"),
    2,
    preprocessor$sds,
    "/"
  )
}

# Model C replaces continuous prior-year giving with fixed, interpretable
# bands. The $60-or-less band is the reference level. A $600 indicator is
# included only when that amount occurs in the corresponding training window.
make_threshold_feature_matrix <- function(
  data,
  training_medians,
  include_common_600
) {
  transformed <- impute_and_transform_ridge_features(data, training_medians)
  prior_year_giving <- as.numeric(data$giving_last_12m)
  prior_year_giving[is.na(prior_year_giving)] <-
    training_medians[["giving_last_12m"]]

  threshold_features <- cbind(
    transformed[, setdiff(colnames(transformed), "giving_last_12m"), drop = FALSE],
    giving_band_61_120 = as.numeric(
      prior_year_giving >= 61 & prior_year_giving <= 120
    ),
    giving_band_121_240 = as.numeric(
      prior_year_giving >= 121 & prior_year_giving <= 240
    ),
    giving_band_241_500 = as.numeric(
      prior_year_giving >= 241 & prior_year_giving <= 500
    ),
    giving_band_over_500 = as.numeric(prior_year_giving > 500)
  )

  if (include_common_600) {
    threshold_features <- cbind(
      threshold_features,
      giving_is_exactly_600 = as.numeric(dplyr::near(prior_year_giving, 600))
    )
  }

  threshold_features
}

fit_threshold_preprocessor <- function(training_data) {
  ridge_preprocessor <- fit_ridge_preprocessor(training_data)
  include_common_600 <- any(
    dplyr::near(training_data$giving_last_12m, 600),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  threshold_training <- make_threshold_feature_matrix(
    training_data,
    ridge_preprocessor$medians,
    include_common_600
  )
  threshold_means <- colMeans(threshold_training)
  threshold_sds <- apply(threshold_training, 2, sd)
  threshold_sds[is.na(threshold_sds) | threshold_sds == 0] <- 1

  list(
    medians = ridge_preprocessor$medians,
    include_common_600 = include_common_600,
    means = threshold_means,
    sds = threshold_sds
  )
}

apply_threshold_preprocessor <- function(data, preprocessor) {
  threshold_features <- make_threshold_feature_matrix(
    data,
    preprocessor$medians,
    preprocessor$include_common_600
  )
  sweep(
    sweep(threshold_features, 2, preprocessor$means, "-"),
    2,
    preprocessor$sds,
    "/"
  )
}

fit_tree_preprocessor <- function(training_data) {
  raw_features <- training_data |>
    select(all_of(ridge_feature_names)) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

  vapply(
    raw_features,
    function(value) {
      median_value <- median(value, na.rm = TRUE)
      if_else(is.na(median_value), 0, median_value)
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
}

apply_tree_preprocessor <- function(data, training_medians) {
  features <- data |>
    select(all_of(ridge_feature_names)) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

  for (feature_name in ridge_feature_names) {
    features[[feature_name]][is.na(features[[feature_name]])] <-
      training_medians[[feature_name]]
  }

  features
}

average_precision <- function(outcome, score) {
  ranked <- tibble(outcome = as.integer(outcome), score = score) |>
    arrange(desc(score)) |>
    mutate(
      rank = row_number(),
      precision_at_rank = cumsum(outcome) / rank
    )

  if (sum(ranked$outcome) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  mean(ranked$precision_at_rank[ranked$outcome == 1])
}

rolling_windows <- tibble(
  test_fiscal_year = paste0("FY", 2022:2024),
  training_fiscal_years = list(
    "FY2021",
    paste0("FY", 2021:2022),
    paste0("FY", 2021:2023)
  )
)

ridge_fit_results <- map(
  seq_len(nrow(rolling_windows)),
  function(window_index) {
    test_year <- rolling_windows$test_fiscal_year[[window_index]]
    train_years <- rolling_windows$training_fiscal_years[[window_index]]

    training_data <- ridge_model_data |>
      filter(snapshot_fiscal_year %in% train_years)
    test_data <- ridge_model_data |>
      filter(snapshot_fiscal_year == test_year)

    preprocessor <- fit_ridge_preprocessor(training_data)
    x_train <- apply_ridge_preprocessor(training_data, preprocessor)
    x_test <- apply_ridge_preprocessor(test_data, preprocessor)

    set.seed(20261021 + window_index)
    ridge_cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
      x = x_train,
      y = as.integer(training_data$converts_to_major_next_fy),
      family = "binomial",
      alpha = 0,
      nfolds = 5,
      type.measure = "deviance",
      standardize = FALSE
    )

    threshold_preprocessor <- fit_threshold_preprocessor(training_data)
    x_threshold_train <- apply_threshold_preprocessor(
      training_data,
      threshold_preprocessor
    )
    x_threshold_test <- apply_threshold_preprocessor(
      test_data,
      threshold_preprocessor
    )

    set.seed(20261121 + window_index)
    threshold_ridge_cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
      x = x_threshold_train,
      y = as.integer(training_data$converts_to_major_next_fy),
      family = "binomial",
      alpha = 0,
      nfolds = 5,
      type.measure = "deviance",
      standardize = FALSE
    )

    tree_medians <- fit_tree_preprocessor(training_data)
    tree_training_data <- apply_tree_preprocessor(training_data, tree_medians) |>
      mutate(
        converts_to_major_next_fy = factor(
          training_data$converts_to_major_next_fy,
          levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)
        )
      )
    tree_test_data <- apply_tree_preprocessor(test_data, tree_medians)

    shallow_tree <- rpart::rpart(
      converts_to_major_next_fy ~ .,
      data = tree_training_data,
      method = "class",
      control = rpart::rpart.control(
        maxdepth = 2,
        minbucket = 200,
        minsplit = 400,
        cp = 0,
        xval = 0
      )
    )

    firth_training_data <- as.data.frame(x_train) |>
      mutate(
        converts_to_major_next_fy = as.integer(
          training_data$converts_to_major_next_fy
        )
      )
    firth_test_data <- as.data.frame(x_test)
    firth_fit <- logistf::logistf(
      converts_to_major_next_fy ~ .,
      data = firth_training_data,
      pl = FALSE
    )

    list(
      scored = test_data |>
        transmute(
          constituent_id,
          snapshot_fiscal_year,
          converts_to_major_next_fy,
          benchmark_score = giving_last_12m,
          ridge_probability = as.numeric(predict(
            ridge_cv,
            newx = x_test,
            s = "lambda.min",
            type = "response"
          )),
          threshold_ridge_probability = as.numeric(predict(
            threshold_ridge_cv,
            newx = x_threshold_test,
            s = "lambda.min",
            type = "response"
          )),
          shallow_tree_probability = predict(
            shallow_tree,
            newdata = tree_test_data,
            type = "prob"
          )[, "TRUE"],
          firth_probability = as.numeric(predict(
            firth_fit,
            newdata = firth_test_data,
            type = "response"
          ))
        ),
      training_audit = tibble(
        test_fiscal_year = test_year,
        training_fiscal_years = paste(train_years, collapse = ", "),
        training_donor_years = nrow(training_data),
        training_events = sum(training_data$converts_to_major_next_fy),
        continuous_ridge_lambda = ridge_cv$lambda.min,
        threshold_ridge_lambda = threshold_ridge_cv$lambda.min,
        common_600_indicator_included = threshold_preprocessor$include_common_600,
        shallow_tree_terminal_nodes = sum(shallow_tree$frame$var == "<leaf>")
      ),
      ridge_cv = ridge_cv,
      threshold_ridge_cv = threshold_ridge_cv,
      shallow_tree = shallow_tree,
      firth_fit = firth_fit
    )
  }
)

ridge_scored_tests <- bind_rows(map(ridge_fit_results, "scored"))
ridge_training_audit <- bind_rows(map(ridge_fit_results, "training_audit"))

ranking_metrics <- function(scored_data, score_column, model_name) {
  ranked <- scored_data |>
    arrange(snapshot_fiscal_year, desc(.data[[score_column]]), constituent_id) |>
    group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
    mutate(rank_within_test = row_number()) |>
    ungroup()

  by_cohort <- ranked |>
    group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
    summarise(
      model = model_name,
      donor_years = n(),
      converters = sum(converts_to_major_next_fy),
      contact_capacity = sum(rank_within_test <= 1000),
      recall_at_1000 = sum(
        converts_to_major_next_fy[rank_within_test <= 1000]
      ) / converters,
      precision_at_1000 = mean(
        converts_to_major_next_fy[rank_within_test <= 1000]
      ),
      lift_at_1000 = precision_at_1000 /
        mean(converts_to_major_next_fy),
      average_precision = average_precision(
        converts_to_major_next_fy,
        .data[[score_column]]
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(test_cohort = snapshot_fiscal_year)

  pooled_selected <- ranked |>
    filter(rank_within_test <= 1000)

  pooled <- tibble(
    snapshot_fiscal_year = NA_character_,
    model = model_name,
    donor_years = nrow(ranked),
    converters = sum(ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    contact_capacity = nrow(pooled_selected),
    recall_at_1000 = sum(pooled_selected$converts_to_major_next_fy) /
      sum(ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    precision_at_1000 = mean(pooled_selected$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    lift_at_1000 = precision_at_1000 /
      mean(ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy),
    average_precision = average_precision(
      ranked$converts_to_major_next_fy,
      ranked[[score_column]]
    ),
    test_cohort = "Pooled (top 1,000 per FY)"
  )

  bind_rows(by_cohort, pooled) |>
    select(test_cohort, model, donor_years, converters, contact_capacity,
           recall_at_1000, precision_at_1000, lift_at_1000, average_precision)
}

Paired bootstrap uncertainty: ridge versus prior-year giving

Uncertainty is estimated from the existing FY2022–FY2024 held-out predictions. Bootstrap resampling is clustered across all test years so that repeated donor appearances remain together. If reciprocal spouse pairs were present, the existing household ID would be the cluster; this release has no supported reciprocal pairs, so the analysis uses donor-level clusters.

Code 
bootstrap_scored_tests <- ridge_scored_tests |>
  left_join(
    household_map |>
      select(constituent_id, household_id, supported_reciprocal_link),
    by = "constituent_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    bootstrap_cluster_id = coalesce(household_id, constituent_id),
    bootstrap_cluster_type = if_else(
      any(supported_reciprocal_link),
      "Household clusters for supported reciprocal spouse pairs",
      "Donor clusters; no supported reciprocal spouse pairs"
    )
  )

bootstrap_cluster_ids <- bootstrap_scored_tests |>
  distinct(bootstrap_cluster_id) |>
  arrange(bootstrap_cluster_id) |>
  pull(bootstrap_cluster_id)

bootstrap_scored_tests <- bootstrap_scored_tests |>
  mutate(
    bootstrap_cluster_index = match(
      bootstrap_cluster_id,
      bootstrap_cluster_ids
    )
  )

bootstrap_records_by_year <- split(
  bootstrap_scored_tests,
  bootstrap_scored_tests$snapshot_fiscal_year
)

top_k_selection <- function(data, cluster_weights, score_column, top_k = 1000L) {
  record_weights <- cluster_weights[data$bootstrap_cluster_index]
  ranked_order <- order(-data[[score_column]], data$constituent_id)
  ranked_weights <- record_weights[ranked_order]
  ranked_outcomes <- as.integer(
    data$converts_to_major_next_fy[ranked_order]
  )
  contact_capacity <- min(top_k, sum(ranked_weights))
  selected_copies <- pmax(
    pmin(
      ranked_weights,
      contact_capacity - c(0, head(cumsum(ranked_weights), -1))
    ),
    0
  )

  c(
    donor_years = sum(ranked_weights),
    converters = sum(ranked_weights * ranked_outcomes),
    contact_capacity = contact_capacity,
    selected_converters = sum(selected_copies * ranked_outcomes)
  )
}

paired_bootstrap_draw <- function() {
  cluster_weights <- tabulate(
    sample.int(
      length(bootstrap_cluster_ids),
      size = length(bootstrap_cluster_ids),
      replace = TRUE
    ),
    nbins = length(bootstrap_cluster_ids)
  )

  benchmark_counts <- Reduce(
    `+`,
    lapply(
      bootstrap_records_by_year,
      top_k_selection,
      cluster_weights = cluster_weights,
      score_column = "benchmark_score"
    )
  )
  ridge_counts <- Reduce(
    `+`,
    lapply(
      bootstrap_records_by_year,
      top_k_selection,
      cluster_weights = cluster_weights,
      score_column = "ridge_probability"
    )
  )
  threshold_ridge_counts <- Reduce(
    `+`,
    lapply(
      bootstrap_records_by_year,
      top_k_selection,
      cluster_weights = cluster_weights,
      score_column = "threshold_ridge_probability"
    )
  )
  shallow_tree_counts <- Reduce(
    `+`,
    lapply(
      bootstrap_records_by_year,
      top_k_selection,
      cluster_weights = cluster_weights,
      score_column = "shallow_tree_probability"
    )
  )
  firth_counts <- Reduce(
    `+`,
    lapply(
      bootstrap_records_by_year,
      top_k_selection,
      cluster_weights = cluster_weights,
      score_column = "firth_probability"
    )
  )

  base_rate <- benchmark_counts[["converters"]] /
    benchmark_counts[["donor_years"]]
  benchmark_recall <- benchmark_counts[["selected_converters"]] /
    benchmark_counts[["converters"]]
  benchmark_precision <- benchmark_counts[["selected_converters"]] /
    benchmark_counts[["contact_capacity"]]

  model_differences <- function(model_counts, model_name) {
    model_recall <- model_counts[["selected_converters"]] /
      model_counts[["converters"]]
    model_precision <- model_counts[["selected_converters"]] /
      model_counts[["contact_capacity"]]

    c(
      setNames(
        model_recall - benchmark_recall,
        paste0(model_name, "__recall_at_1000_difference")
      ),
      setNames(
        model_precision - benchmark_precision,
        paste0(model_name, "__precision_at_1000_difference")
      ),
      setNames(
        model_precision / base_rate - benchmark_precision / base_rate,
        paste0(model_name, "__lift_at_1000_difference")
      )
    )
  }

  c(
    model_differences(ridge_counts, "Continuous ridge"),
    model_differences(threshold_ridge_counts, "Threshold-aware ridge"),
    model_differences(shallow_tree_counts, "Shallow tree"),
    model_differences(firth_counts, "Firth logistic")
  )
}

set.seed(20261022)
paired_bootstrap_differences <- t(replicate(2000, paired_bootstrap_draw())) |>
  as_tibble()

paired_bootstrap_summary <- paired_bootstrap_differences |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = c("model", "metric"),
    names_sep = "__",
    values_to = "ridge_minus_benchmark"
  ) |>
  group_by(model, metric) |>
  summarise(
    paired_difference = mean(ridge_minus_benchmark),
    interval_low = quantile(ridge_minus_benchmark, 0.025),
    interval_high = quantile(ridge_minus_benchmark, 0.975),
    proportion_ridge_better = mean(ridge_minus_benchmark > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      recall_at_1000_difference = "Recall@1,000",
      precision_at_1000_difference = "Precision@1,000",
      lift_at_1000_difference = "Lift@1,000"
    )
  )

# Coefficients are from the largest pre-FY2024 rolling training window. Inputs
# were standardized using that window's training data, so signs are comparable;
# magnitudes remain descriptive because predictors are correlated.
ridge_coefficient_matrix <- as.matrix(coef(
  ridge_fit_results[[3]]$ridge_cv,
  s = "lambda.min"
))

ridge_feature_directions <- tibble(
  feature = rownames(ridge_coefficient_matrix),
  standardized_coefficient = as.numeric(ridge_coefficient_matrix[, 1])
) |>
  filter(feature != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    direction = if_else(
      standardized_coefficient > 0,
      "Higher predicted conversion",
      "Lower predicted conversion"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(standardized_coefficient)))

firth_feature_directions <- tibble(
  feature = names(ridge_fit_results[[3]]$firth_fit$coefficients),
  standardized_coefficient = as.numeric(
    ridge_fit_results[[3]]$firth_fit$coefficients
  )
) |>
  filter(feature != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    direction = if_else(
      standardized_coefficient > 0,
      "Higher predicted conversion",
      "Lower predicted conversion"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(standardized_coefficient)))

largest_window_tree <- ridge_fit_results[[3]]$shallow_tree
shallow_tree_split_rules <- if (is.null(largest_window_tree$splits)) {
  tibble(rule = "No split selected")
} else {
  tibble(
    feature = rownames(largest_window_tree$splits),
    split_point = largest_window_tree$splits[, "index"]
  ) |>
    mutate(
      rule = paste0(feature, " < ", scales::comma(split_point, accuracy = 0.01))
    ) |>
    select(rule)
}

Campaign-history features

Campaign history may reflect both donor engagement and staff targeting. The summaries below are therefore descriptive associations, not evidence that a campaign caused a future major gift.

Code 
# Build campaign features efficiently from constituent × fiscal-year summaries.
# Do not join raw campaign records to the donor-year target panel.

candidate_base <- conversion_12m_panel |>
  mutate(
    snapshot_year_number = as.integer(str_remove(snapshot_fiscal_year, "FY")),
    snapshot_end_date = as.Date(paste0(snapshot_year_number, "-06-30"))
  )

candidate_ids <- candidate_base |>
  distinct(constituent_id)

# Keep only columns needed for campaign features and only relevant constituents.
campaign_history_small <- campaign_members_analysis |>
  select(constituent_id, marketing_code, campaign_start_date, responded_date) |>
  semi_join(candidate_ids, by = "constituent_id") |>
  left_join(
    campaign_codes_analysis |>
      select(marketing_code, communication_method),
    by = "marketing_code"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    campaign_start_date = as.Date(campaign_start_date),
    responded_date = as.Date(responded_date),
    campaign_fy_number = fiscal_year_from_date(campaign_start_date),
    response_fy_number = fiscal_year_from_date(responded_date)
  )

# Aggregate solicitations once by constituent and fiscal year.
campaign_by_fiscal_year <- campaign_history_small |>
  filter(!is.na(campaign_start_date)) |>
  arrange(constituent_id, campaign_start_date, marketing_code) |>
  group_by(constituent_id, campaign_fy_number) |>
  summarise(
    fiscal_year_solicitations = n(),
    communication_method_in_fy = last(
      communication_method[!is.na(communication_method)],
      default = NA_character_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Aggregate responses once by response fiscal year.
# Response timing, not campaign-start timing, determines whether it was known.
responses_by_fiscal_year <- campaign_history_small |>
  filter(!is.na(responded_date)) |>
  group_by(constituent_id, response_fy_number) |>
  summarise(
    fiscal_year_responses = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

campaign_runtime <- system.time({

  campaign_features <- map_dfr(
    sort(unique(candidate_base$snapshot_year_number)),
    function(snapshot_year_number) {

      candidates <- candidate_base |>
        filter(snapshot_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number)

      solicitation_summary <- campaign_by_fiscal_year |>
        filter(campaign_fy_number <= .env$snapshot_year_number) |>
        group_by(constituent_id) |>
        summarise(
          solicitations_last_12m = sum(
            fiscal_year_solicitations[
              campaign_fy_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          solicitations_last_36m = sum(
            fiscal_year_solicitations[
              campaign_fy_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 2
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          lifetime_solicitations = sum(fiscal_year_solicitations, na.rm = TRUE),
          most_recent_communication_method = last(
            communication_method_in_fy[
              !is.na(communication_method_in_fy)
            ],
            default = NA_character_
          ),
          .groups = "drop"
        )

      response_summary <- responses_by_fiscal_year |>
        filter(response_fy_number <= .env$snapshot_year_number) |>
        group_by(constituent_id) |>
        summarise(
          campaign_responses_last_12m = sum(
            fiscal_year_responses[
              response_fy_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          lifetime_campaign_responses = sum(
            fiscal_year_responses,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
          .groups = "drop"
        )

      candidates |>
        left_join(solicitation_summary, by = "constituent_id") |>
        left_join(response_summary, by = "constituent_id") |>
        mutate(
          solicitations_last_12m = replace_na(
            solicitations_last_12m, 0L
          ),
          solicitations_last_36m = replace_na(
            solicitations_last_36m, 0L
          ),
          lifetime_solicitations = replace_na(
            lifetime_solicitations, 0L
          ),
          campaign_responses_last_12m = replace_na(
            campaign_responses_last_12m, 0L
          ),
          lifetime_campaign_responses = replace_na(
            lifetime_campaign_responses, 0L
          ),
          lifetime_campaign_response_rate = if_else(
            lifetime_solicitations > 0,
            lifetime_campaign_responses / lifetime_solicitations,
            NA_real_
          ),
          responded_to_any_campaign_last_12m =
            campaign_responses_last_12m > 0
        )
    }
  )
})
