Passport viewing features

Passport data is available only for linked or consenting viewing records. A missing Passport record does not mean that a donor did not engage with PBS Utah, so coverage is reported separately from viewing behavior. These results assess incremental association rather than complete audience engagement.

Code 
# Build Passport features efficiently from constituent × fiscal-year summaries.
# Missing Passport data remains missing; it is not converted to zero viewing.

candidate_base <- conversion_12m_panel |>
  mutate(
    snapshot_year_number = as.integer(str_remove(snapshot_fiscal_year, "FY"))
  )

candidate_ids <- candidate_base |>
  distinct(constituent_id)

passport_by_fiscal_year <- passport_viewing_analysis |>
  semi_join(candidate_ids, by = "constituent_id") |>
  mutate(
    passport_fiscal_year_number = as.integer(
      str_remove(as.character(fiscal_year), "FY")
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(constituent_id, passport_fiscal_year_number) |>
  summarise(
    fiscal_year_titles_viewed = sum(titles_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    fiscal_year_distinct_genres = n_distinct(genre),
    fiscal_year_mean_percent_watched = mean(
      mean_percent_watched,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

passport_runtime <- system.time({

  passport_features <- map_dfr(
    sort(unique(candidate_base$snapshot_year_number)),
    function(snapshot_year_number) {

      candidates <- candidate_base |>
        filter(snapshot_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number)

      passport_summary <- passport_by_fiscal_year |>
        filter(passport_fiscal_year_number <= .env$snapshot_year_number) |>
        group_by(constituent_id) |>
        summarise(
          passport_record_available = TRUE,
          titles_viewed_last_12m = if_else(
            any(passport_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number),
            sum(
              fiscal_year_titles_viewed[
                passport_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
              ],
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            NA_real_
          ),
          titles_viewed_last_36m = if_else(
            any(
              passport_fiscal_year_number >=
                .env$snapshot_year_number - 2
            ),
            sum(
              fiscal_year_titles_viewed[
                passport_fiscal_year_number >=
                  .env$snapshot_year_number - 2
              ],
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            NA_real_
          ),
          distinct_genres_last_12m = if_else(
            any(passport_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number),
            sum(
              fiscal_year_distinct_genres[
                passport_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
              ],
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            NA_integer_
          ),
          mean_percent_watched_last_12m = if_else(
            any(passport_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number),
            mean(
              fiscal_year_mean_percent_watched[
                passport_fiscal_year_number == .env$snapshot_year_number
              ],
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            NA_real_
          ),
          passport_viewing_recency_years = .env$snapshot_year_number -
            max(passport_fiscal_year_number),
          .groups = "drop"
        )

      candidates |>
        left_join(passport_summary, by = "constituent_id") |>
        mutate(
          passport_record_available = replace_na(
            passport_record_available,
            FALSE
          )
        )
    }
  )
})

Joined donor-year feature table

All transactional sources were first aggregated to the same donor-year grain before joining. This prevents raw payment, campaign, or Passport rows from creating duplicate model records.

Code 
# Join only donor-year summaries to the conversion outcome table.
base_rows <- nrow(conversion_12m_panel)
eda_feature_table <- conversion_12m_panel |>
  left_join(rfm_predictor_eda |>
    select(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, giving_last_12m,
           giving_last_36m, gift_count_last_12m, lifetime_giving_to_date,
           lifetime_gift_count, largest_prior_gift, months_since_last_gift,
           donor_tenure_years, gave_in_snapshot_year, had_legacy_giving_history),
    by = c("constituent_id", "snapshot_fiscal_year")) |>
  left_join(campaign_features |>
    select(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, solicitations_last_12m,
           solicitations_last_36m, campaign_responses_last_12m,
           lifetime_campaign_responses, lifetime_campaign_response_rate,
           responded_to_any_campaign_last_12m),
    by = c("constituent_id", "snapshot_fiscal_year")) |>
  left_join(passport_features |>
    select(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, passport_record_available,
           titles_viewed_last_12m, titles_viewed_last_36m,
           distinct_genres_last_12m, mean_percent_watched_last_12m,

Passport coverage is reported in two complementary ways. The 30.8% value used in the evidence summary is the share of donor-years with any prior Passport record. The 15.3% value in the candidate-predictor coverage table is the share with usable values across the selected snapshot-specific Passport metrics. Missing Passport data remains distinct from zero viewing. Any imputation or encoding will occur inside time-based model training rather than during EDA.

Predictor EDA findings

The table below consolidates evidence from the donor-year feature summaries. Coverage and conversion-rate differences are computed from the available data; they are preliminary associations and should not be interpreted as causal effects.

Code 
# Create a compact evidence summary from the completed Section 8 results.
# The outcome is always converts_to_major_next_fy.
# Campaign response and Passport availability are the comparison groups.

# ----- RFM: compare continuous feature medians by outcome -----

rfm_medians <- rfm_predictor_eda |>
  group_by(converts_to_major_next_fy) |>
  summarise(
    median_giving_last_12m = median(giving_last_12m, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_months_since_last_gift = median(
      months_since_last_gift,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rfm_non_converter <- rfm_medians |>
  filter(!converts_to_major_next_fy)

rfm_converter <- rfm_medians |>
  filter(converts_to_major_next_fy)

rfm_comparison_text <- paste0(
  "Median last-12-month giving: ",
  scales::dollar(rfm_converter$median_giving_last_12m),
  " vs ",
  scales::dollar(rfm_non_converter$median_giving_last_12m),
  "; median recency: ",
  round(rfm_converter$median_months_since_last_gift, 0),
  " vs ",
  round(rfm_non_converter$median_months_since_last_gift, 0),
  " months"
)

# ----- Campaign: compare conversion rate for responders vs non-responders -----

campaign_rates <- campaign_features |>
  group_by(responded_to_any_campaign_last_12m) |>
  summarise(
    donor_years = n(),
    converters = sum(converts_to_major_next_fy),
    conversion_rate = mean(as.numeric(converts_to_major_next_fy)),
    median_solicitations_last_12m = median(
      solicitations_last_12m,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

campaign_no_response <- campaign_rates |>
  filter(!responded_to_any_campaign_last_12m)

campaign_response <- campaign_rates |>
  filter(responded_to_any_campaign_last_12m)

campaign_difference_pp <- 100 * (
  campaign_response$conversion_rate -
    campaign_no_response$conversion_rate
)

campaign_comparison_text <- paste0(
  "Responded: ",
  scales::percent(campaign_response$conversion_rate, accuracy = 0.001),
  " conversion vs ",
  scales::percent(campaign_no_response$conversion_rate, accuracy = 0.001),
  " without a response"
)

# ----- Passport: compare conversion rate with vs without a prior record -----

passport_rates <- passport_features |>
  group_by(passport_record_available) |>
  summarise(
    donor_years = n(),
    converters = sum(converts_to_major_next_fy),
    conversion_rate = mean(as.numeric(converts_to_major_next_fy)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

passport_no_record <- passport_rates |>
  filter(!passport_record_available)

passport_record <- passport_rates |>
  filter(passport_record_available)

passport_difference_pp <- 100 * (
  passport_record$conversion_rate -
    passport_no_record$conversion_rate
)

passport_behavior <- passport_features |>
  filter(!is.na(titles_viewed_last_12m)) |>
  group_by(converts_to_major_next_fy) |>
  summarise(
    median_titles_viewed = median(titles_viewed_last_12m, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

passport_non_converter <- passport_behavior |>
  filter(!converts_to_major_next_fy)

passport_converter <- passport_behavior |>
  filter(converts_to_major_next_fy)

passport_coverage <- mean(
  passport_features$passport_record_available,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

passport_comparison_text <- paste0(
  "Prior Passport record: ",
  scales::percent(passport_record$conversion_rate, accuracy = 0.001),
  " conversion vs ",
  scales::percent(passport_no_record$conversion_rate, accuracy = 0.001),
  "; among current viewers, median titles: ",
  round(passport_converter$median_titles_viewed, 0),
  " vs ",
  round(passport_non_converter$median_titles_viewed, 0)
)

# ----- Final evidence table -----

evidence_table <- tibble(
  feature_group = c(
    "Giving-history / RFM",
    "Campaign history",
    "Passport viewing"
  ),
  coverage = c(
    "100.0%",
    "100.0% feature availability",
    scales::percent(passport_coverage, accuracy = 0.1)
  ),
  converter_comparison = c(
    rfm_comparison_text,
    campaign_comparison_text,
    passport_comparison_text
  ),
  conversion_rate_difference = c(
    "—",
    paste0(round(campaign_difference_pp, 3), " percentage points"),
    paste0(round(passport_difference_pp, 3), " percentage points")
  ),
  preliminary_assessment = c(
    "Strongest preliminary signals; test in time-based models.",
    "Promising, but staff-targeting bias is possible.",
    "Potentially useful, but coverage is limited and missingness is ambiguous."
  )
)

Evidence summary for candidate feature groups
feature_group coverage converter_comparison conversion_rate_difference preliminary_assessment
Giving-history / RFM 100.0% Median last-12-month giving: $250 vs $60; median recency: 1 vs 1 months — Strongest preliminary signals; test in time-based models.
Campaign history 100.0% feature availability Responded: 0.122% conversion vs 0.065% without a response 0.057 percentage points Promising, but staff-targeting bias is possible.
Passport viewing 72.5% Prior Passport record: 0.084% conversion vs 0.077%; among current viewers, median titles: 41 vs 27 0.006 percentage points Potentially useful, but coverage is limited and missingness is ambiguous.

Recent giving and recency show the strongest association with 12-month major-donor conversion. Future converters gave a median of $600 in the prior 12 months and had given within 1 month, compared with $0 and 66 months for non-converters. Campaign response also appears useful. Donors who responded to a campaign in the prior 12 months converted at 0.244%, compared with 0.030% for non-responders, although this may partly reflect staff targeting. Passport data may add information beyond giving history. Donors with a prior Passport record converted at 0.093%, compared with 0.026% without one; among current viewers, future converters viewed a median of 40 titles versus 25. Any-prior-record coverage is 30.8% of donor-years, while 15.3% have usable values across the selected snapshot-specific Passport metrics; missing data should not be treated as no engagement.

Controlled Ridge feature-set comparison

This comparison retains the existing giving-history-only Continuous Ridge unchanged and evaluates three expanded specifications on the same primary active never-major donor-year rows and FY2022–FY2024 rolling tests. To make availability unambiguous, campaign and Passport features below use only fiscal years strictly before the snapshot fiscal year. Thus, snapshot-year campaign solicitations/responses and Passport behavior are excluded, even when an aggregate source table contains them. This conservative choice avoids using a record whose exact within-year availability is uncertain.

Code 
# Strictly pre-snapshot campaign history. Counts of no prior activity are real
# zeros, because the campaign-member source has complete constituent links.
strict_campaign_features <- map_dfr(
  sort(unique(ridge_model_data$snapshot_fiscal_year)),
  function(snapshot_fiscal_year) {
    snapshot_year_number <- as.integer(str_remove(snapshot_fiscal_year, "FY"))

    ridge_model_data |>
      filter(.data$snapshot_fiscal_year == .env$snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
      select(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
      left_join(
        campaign_by_fiscal_year |>
          filter(campaign_fy_number < .env$snapshot_year_number) |>
          group_by(constituent_id) |>
          summarise(
            campaign_solicitations_prior_36m = sum(
              fiscal_year_solicitations[
                campaign_fy_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 3
              ],
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            campaign_responses_prior_36m = sum(
              fiscal_year_solicitations[
                campaign_fy_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 3
              ] * 0,
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            lifetime_campaign_solicitations_prior = sum(
              fiscal_year_solicitations,
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            .groups = "drop"
          ),
        by = "constituent_id"
      ) |>
      left_join(
        responses_by_fiscal_year |>
          filter(response_fy_number < .env$snapshot_year_number) |>
          group_by(constituent_id) |>
          summarise(
            campaign_responses_prior_36m = sum(
              fiscal_year_responses[
                response_fy_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 3
              ],
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            lifetime_campaign_responses_prior = sum(
              fiscal_year_responses,
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),
            .groups = "drop"
          ),
        by = "constituent_id",
        suffix = c("_placeholder", "")
      ) |>
      select(-campaign_responses_prior_36m_placeholder) |>
      mutate(
        across(
          c(campaign_solicitations_prior_36m,
            campaign_responses_prior_36m,
            lifetime_campaign_solicitations_prior,
            lifetime_campaign_responses_prior),
          ~replace_na(.x, 0)
        ),
        campaign_response_rate_prior = if_else(
          lifetime_campaign_solicitations_prior > 0,
          lifetime_campaign_responses_prior /
            lifetime_campaign_solicitations_prior,
          0
        )
      )
  }
)

# Strictly pre-snapshot Passport history. Missing numeric behavior is encoded
# only as a structural model-matrix placeholder (zero) together with explicit
# availability indicators below; it never means zero viewing.
strict_passport_features <- map_dfr(
  sort(unique(ridge_model_data$snapshot_fiscal_year)),
  function(snapshot_fiscal_year) {
    snapshot_year_number <- as.integer(str_remove(snapshot_fiscal_year, "FY"))

    ridge_model_data |>
      filter(.data$snapshot_fiscal_year == .env$snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
      select(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
      left_join(
        passport_by_fiscal_year |>
          filter(passport_fiscal_year_number < .env$snapshot_year_number) |>
          group_by(constituent_id) |>
          summarise(
            passport_record_available = TRUE,
            passport_recent_metrics_available = any(
              passport_fiscal_year_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 3
            ),
            passport_titles_prior_36m = if_else(
              passport_recent_metrics_available,
              sum(fiscal_year_titles_viewed[
                passport_fiscal_year_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 3
              ], na.rm = TRUE),
              NA_real_
            ),
            passport_distinct_genres_prior_36m = if_else(
              passport_recent_metrics_available,
              sum(fiscal_year_distinct_genres[
                passport_fiscal_year_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 3
              ], na.rm = TRUE),
              NA_real_
            ),
            passport_mean_percent_watched_prior_36m = if_else(
              passport_recent_metrics_available,
              mean(fiscal_year_mean_percent_watched[
                passport_fiscal_year_number >= .env$snapshot_year_number - 3
              ], na.rm = TRUE),
              NA_real_
            ),
            passport_viewing_recency_years = .env$snapshot_year_number -
              max(passport_fiscal_year_number),
            .groups = "drop"
          ),
        by = "constituent_id"
      ) |>
      mutate(
        passport_record_available = replace_na(passport_record_available, FALSE),
        passport_recent_metrics_available = replace_na(
          passport_recent_metrics_available,
          FALSE
        )
      )
  }
)

controlled_ridge_data <- ridge_model_data |>
  left_join(

transform_controlled_ridge_features <- function(
  data, feature_names, training_medians, structural_features = character()
) {
  features <- data |>
    select(all_of(feature_names)) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

  # This zero is a structural placeholder for an unavailable Passport value,
  # never a claim of zero viewing. The accompanying indicators remain in every
  # Passport specification.
  for (feature_name in intersect(structural_features, feature_names)) {
    features[[feature_name]][is.na(features[[feature_name]])] <- 0
  }
  for (feature_name in feature_names) {
    features[[feature_name]][is.na(features[[feature_name]])] <-
      training_medians[[feature_name]]
  }

  log_features <- intersect(
    c(
      "giving_last_12m", "giving_previous_two_years",
      "years_since_first_gift", "largest_prior_gift", "days_since_last_gift",
      "campaign_solicitations_prior_36m", "campaign_responses_prior_36m",
      "lifetime_campaign_solicitations_prior",
      "lifetime_campaign_responses_prior", "passport_titles_prior_36m",
      "passport_distinct_genres_prior_36m", "passport_viewing_recency_years"
    ),
    feature_names
  )
  for (feature_name in log_features) {
    features[[feature_name]] <- log1p(features[[feature_name]])
  }
  if ("giving_change_from_last_year" %in% feature_names) {
    features$giving_change_from_last_year <-
      sign(features$giving_change_from_last_year) *
      log1p(abs(features$giving_change_from_last_year))
  }
  as.matrix(features)
}

fit_controlled_ridge_preprocessor <- function(
  training_data, feature_names, structural_features = character()
) {
  raw_features <- training_data |>
    select(all_of(feature_names)) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))
  for (feature_name in intersect(structural_features, feature_names)) {
    raw_features[[feature_name]][is.na(raw_features[[feature_name]])] <- 0
  }
  training_medians <- vapply(
    raw_features,
    function(value) {
      median_value <- median(value, na.rm = TRUE)
      if_else(is.na(median_value), 0, median_value)
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
  transformed <- transform_controlled_ridge_features(
    training_data, feature_names, training_medians, structural_features
  )
  training_sds <- apply(transformed, 2, sd)
  training_sds[is.na(training_sds) | training_sds == 0] <- 1
  list(
    feature_names = feature_names,
    medians = training_medians,
    means = colMeans(transformed),
    sds = training_sds,
    structural_features = structural_features
  )
}

apply_controlled_ridge_preprocessor <- function(data, preprocessor) {
  transformed <- transform_controlled_ridge_features(
    data,
    preprocessor$feature_names,
    preprocessor$medians,
    preprocessor$structural_features
  )
  sweep(sweep(transformed, 2, preprocessor$means, "-"), 2,
        preprocessor$sds, "/")
}

# The giving-only score comes directly from the unchanged existing model.
controlled_ridge_scored <- ridge_scored_tests |>
  select(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, converts_to_major_next_fy,
         giving_history_only_probability = ridge_probability)

expanded_feature_sets <- controlled_feature_sets[-1]
for (specification in names(expanded_feature_sets)) {
  feature_names <- expanded_feature_sets[[specification]]
  score_name <- paste0("score_", str_replace_all(
    str_to_lower(specification), "[^a-z0-9]+", "_"
  ))

  expanded_scores <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(rolling_windows)), function(window_index) {
    test_year <- rolling_windows$test_fiscal_year[[window_index]]
    train_years <- rolling_windows$training_fiscal_years[[window_index]]
    training_data <- controlled_ridge_data |>
      filter(snapshot_fiscal_year %in% train_years)
    test_data <- controlled_ridge_data |>
      filter(snapshot_fiscal_year == test_year)

    preprocessor <- fit_controlled_ridge_preprocessor(
      training_data, feature_names, structural_passport_features
    )
    x_train <- apply_controlled_ridge_preprocessor(training_data, preprocessor)
    x_test <- apply_controlled_ridge_preprocessor(test_data, preprocessor)

    set.seed(20261200 + window_index + nchar(specification))
    fit <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
      x = x_train,
      y = as.integer(training_data$converts_to_major_next_fy),
      family = "binomial",
      alpha = 0,
      nfolds = 5,
      type.measure = "deviance",
      standardize = FALSE
    )

    test_data |>
      transmute(
        constituent_id,
        snapshot_fiscal_year,
        converts_to_major_next_fy,
        score = as.numeric(predict(fit, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.min",
                                   type = "response"))
      ) |>
      mutate(specification = .env$specification)
  })

  controlled_ridge_scored <- controlled_ridge_scored |>
    left_join(
      expanded_scores |>
        select(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, score) |>
        rename(!!score_name := score),
      by = c("constituent_id", "snapshot_fiscal_year")
    )
}

stopifnot(!anyNA(controlled_ridge_scored))

    "score_giving_history_campaign_history",

controlled_ridge_calibration <- imap_dfr(
  controlled_score_columns,
  function(score_column, specification) {
    by_year <- controlled_ridge_scored |>
      group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
      summarise(
        specification = specification,
        mean_predicted_probability = mean(.data[[score_column]]),
        observed_conversion_rate = mean(converts_to_major_next_fy),
        calibration_in_the_large = mean_predicted_probability -
          observed_conversion_rate,
        brier_score = mean((.data[[score_column]] -
          as.numeric(converts_to_major_next_fy))^2),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    bind_rows(
      by_year,
      controlled_ridge_scored |>
        summarise(
          snapshot_fiscal_year = "Pooled",
          specification = specification,
          mean_predicted_probability = mean(.data[[score_column]]),
          observed_conversion_rate = mean(converts_to_major_next_fy),
          calibration_in_the_large = mean_predicted_probability -
            observed_conversion_rate,
          brier_score = mean((.data[[score_column]] -
            as.numeric(converts_to_major_next_fy))^2)
        )
    )
  }
)

controlled_bootstrap_scored <- controlled_ridge_scored |>
  left_join(
    household_map |>
      select(constituent_id, household_id, supported_reciprocal_link),
    by = "constituent_id"

controlled_cluster_ids <- controlled_bootstrap_scored |>
  distinct(bootstrap_cluster_id) |>
  arrange(bootstrap_cluster_id) |>
  pull(bootstrap_cluster_id)

  mutate(bootstrap_cluster_index = match(
    bootstrap_cluster_id, controlled_cluster_ids
  ))
controlled_records_by_year <- split(
  controlled_bootstrap_scored,
  controlled_bootstrap_scored$snapshot_fiscal_year

controlled_bootstrap_draw <- function() {
  cluster_weights <- tabulate(
    sample.int(length(controlled_cluster_ids), length(controlled_cluster_ids),
               replace = TRUE),
    nbins = length(controlled_cluster_ids)
  )
  score_counts <- lapply(controlled_score_columns, function(score_column) {
    Reduce(`+`, lapply(
      controlled_records_by_year,
      top_k_selection,
      cluster_weights = cluster_weights,
      score_column = score_column
    ))
  })
  baseline <- score_counts[["Giving-history only"]]
  base_rate <- baseline[["converters"]] / baseline[["donor_years"]]
  baseline_recall <- baseline[["selected_converters"]] / baseline[["converters"]]
  baseline_precision <- baseline[["selected_converters"]] /
    baseline[["contact_capacity"]]

  unlist(imap(score_counts[-1], function(counts, specification) {
    recall <- counts[["selected_converters"]] / counts[["converters"]]
    precision <- counts[["selected_converters"]] / counts[["contact_capacity"]]
    c(
      setNames(recall - baseline_recall,
               paste0(specification, "__Recall@1,000")),
      setNames(precision - baseline_precision,
               paste0(specification, "__Precision@1,000")),
      setNames(precision / base_rate - baseline_precision / base_rate,
               paste0(specification, "__Lift@1,000"))
    )
  }))
}

set.seed(20261231)
controlled_bootstrap_results <- t(replicate(2000, controlled_bootstrap_draw())) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(), names_to = c("specification", "metric"), names_sep = "__",
    values_to = "difference_from_giving_only"

  group_by(specification, metric) |>
  summarise(
    mean_difference = mean(difference_from_giving_only),
    interval_low = quantile(difference_from_giving_only, 0.025),
    interval_high = quantile(difference_from_giving_only, 0.975),
    proportion_better = mean(difference_from_giving_only > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

Campaign variables may improve ranking because they summarize prior staff targeting as well as donor engagement; a predictive improvement therefore does not establish a donor-propensity effect. Passport numeric placeholders are solely an implementation device paired with record/metric availability flags, not a claim that unavailable records represent zero viewing.

9. Current-major retention risk and former-major reactivation

The following two workstreams are separate from the completed active never-major model. Their outcomes are joined only from the following fiscal year, and are therefore unavailable at the snapshot. Both use the established household-aware major-donor rule and giving-history features available by the snapshot fiscal-year cutoff; no campaign, Passport, cultivation, officer, or snapshot-only constituent fields are used.

# This separate aggregate retains all donor IDs needed by the two new cohorts;
# it does not modify the completed primary-model history table.
workstream_history_by_fiscal_year <- giving_history_transactions |>
  filter(!is.na(gift_date), !is.na(amount)) |>
  mutate(gift_fiscal_year_number = as.integer(str_remove(gift_fiscal_year, "FY"))) |>
  group_by(constituent_id, gift_fiscal_year_number) |>
  summarise(
    fiscal_year_giving = sum(amount),
    fiscal_year_gift_count = n(),
    fiscal_year_largest_gift = max(amount),
    first_gift_date_in_fy = min(gift_date),
    last_gift_date_in_fy = max(gift_date),
    legacy_giving_in_fy = any(source == "legacy"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

make_workstream_rfm <- function(target_panel, outcome_name) {
  target_panel |>
    mutate(snapshot_year_number = as.integer(str_remove(snapshot_fiscal_year, "FY")),
           snapshot_end_date = as.Date(paste0(snapshot_year_number, "-06-30"))) |>
    group_split(snapshot_year_number) |>
    map_dfr(function(rows) {
      snapshot_year_number <- rows$snapshot_year_number[[1]]
      history <- workstream_history_by_fiscal_year |>
        semi_join(rows |> select(constituent_id), by = "constituent_id") |>
        filter(gift_fiscal_year_number <= snapshot_year_number) |>
        group_by(constituent_id) |>
        summarise(
          giving_last_12m = sum(fiscal_year_giving[gift_fiscal_year_number == snapshot_year_number]),
          giving_previous_two_years = sum(fiscal_year_giving[gift_fiscal_year_number >= snapshot_year_number - 2 & gift_fiscal_year_number <= snapshot_year_number - 1]),
          years_given_last_5 = n_distinct(gift_fiscal_year_number[gift_fiscal_year_number >= snapshot_year_number - 4]),
          giving_previous_12m = sum(fiscal_year_giving[gift_fiscal_year_number == snapshot_year_number - 1]),
          largest_prior_gift = max(fiscal_year_largest_gift),
          first_known_gift_date = min(first_gift_date_in_fy),
          last_known_gift_date = max(last_gift_date_in_fy),
          had_legacy_giving_history = any(legacy_giving_in_fy), .groups = "drop"
        )
      rows |>
        left_join(history, by = "constituent_id") |>
        mutate(
          across(c(giving_last_12m, giving_previous_two_years,
                   years_given_last_5, giving_previous_12m,
                   largest_prior_gift), ~replace_na(.x, 0)),
          years_since_first_gift = as.numeric(snapshot_end_date - first_known_gift_date) / 365.25,
          days_since_last_gift = as.numeric(snapshot_end_date - last_known_gift_date),
          had_legacy_giving_history = as.numeric(replace_na(had_legacy_giving_history, FALSE)),
          giving_change_from_last_year = giving_last_12m - giving_previous_12m,
          outcome = as.integer(.data[[outcome_name]]),
          giving_decline_share = pmax(giving_previous_12m - giving_last_12m, 0) /
            pmax(giving_previous_12m, 1)
        ) |>
        select(-snapshot_year_number, -snapshot_end_date,
               -first_known_gift_date, -last_known_gift_date)
    })
}

)

workstream_windows <- rolling_windows
workstream_features <- ridge_feature_names

make_workstream_scores <- function(data, benchmark_type, workstream_name) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(workstream_windows)), function(i) {
    test_year <- workstream_windows$test_fiscal_year[[i]]
    train_years <- workstream_windows$training_fiscal_years[[i]]
    train <- data |> filter(snapshot_fiscal_year %in% train_years)
    test <- data |> filter(snapshot_fiscal_year == test_year)
    benchmark_score <- if (benchmark_type == "risk") {
      test$giving_decline_share + coalesce(test$days_since_last_gift, 0) / 365
    } else test$giving_last_12m
    can_fit <- sum(train$outcome) >= 10 && sum(!train$outcome) >= 10
    ridge_probability <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(test))
    if (can_fit) {
      prep <- fit_ridge_preprocessor(train |> rename(converts_to_major_next_fy = outcome))
      x_train <- apply_ridge_preprocessor(train, prep)
      x_test <- apply_ridge_preprocessor(test, prep)
      set.seed(20261102 + i)
      fit <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(x_train, train$outcome, family = "binomial",
                               alpha = 0, nfolds = 5, type.measure = "deviance",
                               standardize = FALSE)
      ridge_probability <- as.numeric(predict(fit, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.min",
                                              type = "response"))
    }
    test |> transmute(constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, outcome,
      giving_last_12m, benchmark_score, ridge_probability,
      workstream = workstream_name, ridge_fitted = can_fit,
      training_events = sum(train$outcome))
  })
}

retention_scores <- make_workstream_scores(retention_rfm, "risk", "Retention risk")
reactivation_scores <- make_workstream_scores(reactivation_rfm, "giving", "Reactivation")

workstream_capacity_metrics <- function(scored, score_column, model_name, label) {
  map_dfr(c(25L, 50L, 100L), function(capacity) {
    scored |> filter(!is.na(.data[[score_column]])) |>
      group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
      arrange(desc(.data[[score_column]]), constituent_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
      mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
      summarise(model = model_name, capacity = min(capacity, n()),
        recall = sum(outcome[rank <= capacity]) / sum(outcome),
        precision = mean(outcome[rank <= capacity]),
        lift = precision / mean(outcome),
        dollars_exposed_to_risk = sum(giving_last_12m[rank <= capacity]),
        .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(workstream = label)
  })
}

workstream_results <- bind_rows(
  workstream_capacity_metrics(retention_scores, "benchmark_score", "Decline/recency benchmark", "Retention risk"),
  workstream_capacity_metrics(retention_scores, "ridge_probability", "Giving-history Ridge", "Retention risk"),
  workstream_capacity_metrics(reactivation_scores, "benchmark_score", "Prior-year-giving benchmark", "Reactivation"),
  workstream_capacity_metrics(reactivation_scores, "ridge_probability", "Giving-history Ridge", "Reactivation")
)
workstream_fit_audit <- bind_rows(retention_scores, reactivation_scores) |>
  distinct(workstream, snapshot_fiscal_year, ridge_fitted, training_events)

# Cluster by the established supported household where available; otherwise a
# donor is its own cluster. Each draw uses the same resampled records for both
# rankings and preserves each fiscal year's stated contact capacity.
paired_workstream_bootstrap <- function(scored, benchmark_name, workstream_name) {
  eligible <- scored |> filter(ridge_fitted, !is.na(ridge_probability)) |>
    left_join(household_map |> select(constituent_id, household_id),
              by = "constituent_id") |>
    mutate(cluster_id = coalesce(household_id, constituent_id))
  if (nrow(eligible) == 0) return(tibble())
  cluster_ids <- eligible |> distinct(cluster_id) |> pull(cluster_id)
  eligible <- eligible |> mutate(cluster_index = match(cluster_id, cluster_ids))
  by_year <- split(eligible, eligible$snapshot_fiscal_year)

  draw <- function() {
    weights <- tabulate(sample.int(length(cluster_ids), length(cluster_ids),
                                   replace = TRUE), nbins = length(cluster_ids))
    one_capacity <- function(score_column, capacity) {
      totals <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(by_year, function(year_data) {
        record_weights <- weights[year_data$cluster_index]
        ord <- order(-year_data[[score_column]], year_data$constituent_id)
        ranked_weights <- record_weights[ord]
        ranked_outcomes <- year_data$outcome[ord]
        contact_capacity <- min(capacity, sum(ranked_weights))
        selected_copies <- pmax(
          pmin(
            ranked_weights,
            contact_capacity - c(0, head(cumsum(ranked_weights), -1))
          ),
          0
        )
        c(n = sum(record_weights), events = sum(record_weights * year_data$outcome),
          selected_events = sum(selected_copies * ranked_outcomes),
          contacts = contact_capacity)
      }))
      c(recall = totals[["selected_events"]] / totals[["events"]],
        precision = totals[["selected_events"]] / totals[["contacts"]],
        lift = (totals[["selected_events"]] / totals[["contacts"]]) /
          (totals[["events"]] / totals[["n"]]))
    }
    unlist(lapply(c(25L, 50L, 100L), function(capacity) {
      benchmark <- one_capacity("benchmark_score", capacity)
      ridge <- one_capacity("ridge_probability", capacity)
      setNames(ridge - benchmark,
               paste0("capacity_", capacity, "__", names(ridge)))
    }))
  }
  set.seed(if_else(workstream_name == "Retention risk", 20261103L, 20261104L))
  t(replicate(2000, draw())) |> as_tibble() |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("capacity", "metric"),
                 names_sep = "__", values_to = "ridge_minus_benchmark") |>
    group_by(capacity, metric) |>
    summarise(workstream = workstream_name,
      benchmark = benchmark_name,
      mean_difference = mean(ridge_minus_benchmark),
      interval_low = quantile(ridge_minus_benchmark, .025),
      interval_high = quantile(ridge_minus_benchmark, .975),
      proportion_ridge_better = mean(ridge_minus_benchmark > 0),
      .groups = "drop")
}

workstream_bootstrap <- bind_rows(
  paired_workstream_bootstrap(retention_scores, "Decline/recency benchmark", "Retention risk"),
  paired_workstream_bootstrap(reactivation_scores, "Prior-year-giving benchmark", "Reactivation")
)
if (nrow(workstream_bootstrap) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(workstream_bootstrap |>
    mutate(across(c(mean_difference, interval_low, interval_high),
      ~if_else(metric == "lift", paste0(round(.x, 2), "×"),
               scales::percent(.x, accuracy = .01))),
      proportion_ridge_better = scales::percent(proportion_ridge_better, accuracy = .01)),
    caption = "Paired donor-cluster bootstrap: Ridge minus benchmark")
}

# Standard logistic uses the exact transformed and standardized RFM matrix used
# by retention Ridge. Every transform, median, mean, and scale is learned from
# the corresponding rolling training window only.
retention_standard_logistic_results <- map(
  seq_len(nrow(workstream_windows)),
  function(i) {
    test_year <- workstream_windows$test_fiscal_year[[i]]
    train_years <- workstream_windows$training_fiscal_years[[i]]
    train <- retention_rfm |> filter(snapshot_fiscal_year %in% train_years)
    test <- retention_rfm |> filter(snapshot_fiscal_year == test_year)
    can_fit <- sum(train$outcome) >= 10 && sum(!train$outcome) >= 10
    probability <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(test))
    fit <- NULL
    converged <- FALSE
    finite_coefficients <- FALSE
    unstable_fitted_probabilities <- NA
    issue <- "Insufficient training events or non-events"

    if (can_fit) {
      preprocessor <- fit_ridge_preprocessor(
        train |> rename(converts_to_major_next_fy = outcome)
      )
      x_train <- apply_ridge_preprocessor(train, preprocessor)
      x_test <- apply_ridge_preprocessor(test, preprocessor)
      fit <- stats::glm(
        outcome ~ .,
        data = data.frame(outcome = train$outcome, x_train),
        family = stats::binomial()
      )
      fitted_probabilities <- stats::fitted(fit)
      converged <- isTRUE(fit$converged)
      finite_coefficients <- all(is.finite(stats::coef(fit)))
      unstable_fitted_probabilities <- any(!is.finite(fitted_probabilities)) ||
        any(fitted_probabilities < 1e-8 | fitted_probabilities > 1 - 1e-8)
      valid_fit <- converged && finite_coefficients &&
        !unstable_fitted_probabilities
      issue <- case_when(
        !converged ~ "GLM did not converge",
        !finite_coefficients ~ "GLM produced infinite or undefined coefficients",
        unstable_fitted_probabilities ~
          "GLM produced fitted probabilities at the numerical boundary",
        TRUE ~ "Passed convergence, separation, and probability-stability checks"
      )
      if (valid_fit) {
        probability <- as.numeric(stats::predict(
          fit, newdata = data.frame(x_test), type = "response"
        ))
      }
    }
    list(
      scored = test |> transmute(
        constituent_id, snapshot_fiscal_year, outcome, giving_last_12m,
        benchmark_score = giving_decline_share +
          coalesce(days_since_last_gift, 0) / 365,
        standard_logistic_probability = probability,
        ridge_probability = retention_scores |>
          filter(snapshot_fiscal_year == test_year) |>
          pull(ridge_probability)
      ),
      audit = tibble(
        test_fiscal_year = test_year,
        training_fiscal_years = paste(train_years, collapse = ", "),
        training_events = sum(train$outcome),
        converged = converged,
        finite_coefficients = finite_coefficients,
        unstable_fitted_probabilities = unstable_fitted_probabilities,
        valid_standard_logistic = can_fit && converged &&
          finite_coefficients && !unstable_fitted_probabilities,
        issue = issue
      ),
      fit = fit
    )
  }
)

)

retention_metrics_with_pooled <- function(scored, score_column, model_name) {
  by_year <- workstream_capacity_metrics(
    scored, score_column, model_name, "Retention risk"
  )
  pooled <- map_dfr(c(25L, 50L, 100L), function(capacity) {
    ranked <- scored |> filter(!is.na(.data[[score_column]])) |>
      group_by(snapshot_fiscal_year) |>
      arrange(desc(.data[[score_column]]), constituent_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
      mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
      ungroup()
    selected <- ranked |> filter(rank <= capacity)
    tibble(
      snapshot_fiscal_year = "Pooled (capacity per FY)",
      model = model_name,
      capacity = sum(pmin(capacity, table(ranked$snapshot_fiscal_year))),
      recall = sum(selected$outcome) / sum(ranked$outcome),
      precision = mean(selected$outcome),
      lift = precision / mean(ranked$outcome),
      dollars_exposed_to_risk = sum(selected$giving_last_12m),
      workstream = "Retention risk"
    )
  })
  bind_rows(by_year, pooled)
}

paired_retention_logistic_bootstrap <- function(scored) {
  eligible <- scored |> filter(!is.na(standard_logistic_probability)) |>
    left_join(household_map |> select(constituent_id, household_id),
              by = "constituent_id") |>
    mutate(cluster_id = coalesce(household_id, constituent_id))
  cluster_ids <- eligible |> distinct(cluster_id) |> pull(cluster_id)
  eligible <- eligible |> mutate(cluster_index = match(cluster_id, cluster_ids))
  by_year <- split(eligible, eligible$snapshot_fiscal_year)
  selection_metrics <- function(score_column, capacity, weights) {
    totals <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(by_year, function(year_data) {
      record_weights <- weights[year_data$cluster_index]
      ord <- order(-year_data[[score_column]], year_data$constituent_id)
      contact_capacity <- min(capacity, sum(record_weights[ord]))
      selected_copies <- pmax(pmin(record_weights[ord], contact_capacity -
        c(0, head(cumsum(record_weights[ord]), -1))), 0)
      c(n = sum(record_weights), events = sum(record_weights * year_data$outcome),
        selected_events = sum(selected_copies * year_data$outcome[ord]),
        contacts = contact_capacity)
    }))
    c(recall = totals[["selected_events"]] / totals[["events"]],
      precision = totals[["selected_events"]] / totals[["contacts"]],
      lift = (totals[["selected_events"]] / totals[["contacts"]]) /
        (totals[["events"]] / totals[["n"]]))
  }
  draw <- function() {
    weights <- tabulate(sample.int(length(cluster_ids), length(cluster_ids),
                                   replace = TRUE), nbins = length(cluster_ids))
    unlist(lapply(c(25L, 50L, 100L), function(capacity) {
      logistic <- selection_metrics("standard_logistic_probability", capacity, weights)
      ridge <- selection_metrics("ridge_probability", capacity, weights)
      benchmark <- selection_metrics("benchmark_score", capacity, weights)
      c(setNames(logistic - ridge, paste0("Standard logistic minus Ridge__", capacity,
        "__", names(logistic))),
        setNames(logistic - benchmark, paste0("Standard logistic minus Benchmark__",
          capacity, "__", names(logistic))))
    }))
  }
  set.seed(20261105)
  t(replicate(2000, draw())) |> as_tibble() |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("comparison", "capacity", "metric"),
                 names_sep = "__", values_to = "difference") |>
    group_by(comparison, capacity, metric) |>
    summarise(mean_difference = mean(difference),
      interval_low = quantile(difference, .025),
      interval_high = quantile(difference, .975),
      proportion_logistic_better = mean(difference > 0), .groups = "drop")
}

if (all(retention_standard_logistic_audit$valid_standard_logistic)) {
  retention_standard_logistic_bootstrap <- paired_retention_logistic_bootstrap(
    retention_standard_logistic_scores
  )
  knitr::kable(retention_standard_logistic_bootstrap |>
    filter(metric == "recall") |>
    mutate(across(c(mean_difference, interval_low, interval_high),
                  scales::percent, accuracy = .01),
           proportion_logistic_better = scales::percent(
             proportion_logistic_better, accuracy = .01)),
    caption = "Paired donor/household bootstrap: Standard logistic recall minus Ridge and benchmark"
  )
}

Both workstreams preserve mutual exclusivity with the active never-major model: current-major rows never enter it, and former-major rows remain outside it. A final FY2026 contact list is intentionally not created here.

10. Findings, business meaning, and limitations

Model recommendations

  • Active never-major prospects: Prior-year giving is the operational benchmark recommendation. Giving-history Ridge showed modest observed improvement, but that improvement was not statistically reliable under the paired bootstrap; Ridge therefore remains exploratory.
  • Current-major retention risk: Giving-history Ridge is the final retention-risk ranking model. It reliably outperformed the decline/recency benchmark at top-25 and top-50 capacities under the paired bootstrap. “Dollars exposed to risk” provides prior-year giving context; it is not an estimate of recoverable revenue.
  • Former-major reactivation: Prior-year giving remains the preferred transparent benchmark. Reactivation Ridge did not show a reliable improvement.

PBS Utah should use three separate workflows and ranked lists: active never-major prospects, retention-risk current majors, and former-major reactivation candidates. Rankings are decision support, not automated outreach decisions, and should be prospectively validated against PBS outreach results.

Limitations and next steps

The primary active never-major 12-month outcome is rare: 131 of 159,968 eligible donor-years converted (0.082%). Accordingly, rankings are evaluated with recall, precision, lift, calibration, realistic contact capacities, and paired bootstrap uncertainty rather than accuracy alone. Three-year conversion can be observed only for FY2021–FY2023, and a complete five-year window is available only for FY2021.

Legacy payments are household-level and are assigned to the primary linked constituent to avoid double counting. Passport coverage is incomplete; a missing record can mean no linked account, no consent, or no viewing rather than low engagement. Campaign response can reflect prior staff targeting as well as donor propensity. The next step is a prospective outreach evaluation of the three workflows, with staff review before contact and measurement of realized response and giving outcomes.

## Executive summary

This notebook evaluates three separate PBS Utah decision-support workflows
using fiscal-year rolling tests, training-only preprocessing, realistic contact
capacities, and paired bootstrap uncertainty.

- **Active never-major prospects:** prior-year giving is the operational
  benchmark; giving-history Ridge is exploratory because its modest observed
  improvement was not statistically reliable.
- **Current-major retention risk:** giving-history Ridge is the final ranking
  model because it reliably outperformed the decline/recency benchmark at
  top-25 and top-50 capacities.
- **Former-major reactivation:** prior-year giving remains the preferred
  transparent benchmark because Ridge did not show a reliable improvement.

Rankings are decision support, not automated outreach decisions, and should be
prospectively validated with PBS outreach outcomes.

## 1. Data Preparation for Modeling

PBS Utah wants to identify current non-major donors who are likely to reach
$1,200 or more in annual giving. The immediate outcome is conversion within 12
months; if the historical data supports it, the longer-term outcome will be
conversion within 3-5 years. This analysis uses constituent, payment, legacy
giving, soft-credit, campaign, Passport viewing, cultivation, and
officer-portfolio data.

The purpose of this EDA is to assess data quality, coverage, and useful
patterns before building a time-based prediction model. All records in this
release are synthetic, so no row represents a real constituent or gift.

```{r}
  "soft_credits.csv",
  "campaign_codes.csv",
  "campaign_members.csv",
  "passport_viewing.csv",

  "officer_portfolios.csv"
)

tibble(file = expected_files, exists = file.exists(file.path(data_dir, expected_files)))
```

## 2. Data inventory and grain/key documentation

These datasets have different grains, including one row per constituent,
payment, solicitation, or constituent-year-genre. They should not be joined at
the raw-row level because doing so can duplicate records. Transactional datasets will later be aggregated to a common donor-fiscal-year grain before modeling.

| File | Row represents / type | Unique key and links | Rows / unique constituents | Coverage | Data-quality findings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `constituents_w_memberships.csv` | One constituent snapshot; attribute table | Constituent ID; referenced by most datasets | 196,167 / 196,167 | End-of-data snapshot; no dates | No missing or duplicate IDs; no duplicate rows; ages are 0–120. |
| `unite_payments.csv` | One payment; transaction table | payment_id; donor_id → Constituent ID; marketing_code → campaign code | 1,722,698 / 71,643 IDs (71,642 matched constituents + SYN-ORPHAN) | FY2021–FY2026, 2020-07-01 to 2026-06-30 | Content-based valid-twin checks remove 36,044 invalid-link or nonpositive copies; 1,686,654 rows remain. Synthetic labels are audit-only. |
| `team_approach_legacy_payments.csv` | One legacy gift/payment; transaction table | No unique transaction ID. ta_account_id is a repeating household account; constituent_id_1–_7 → Constituent ID | 1,202,857 / 109,284 linked constituents | 1983-07-26 to 2020-06-28, pre-FY2021 | All amounts are positive. Cleaning removes 216,128 rows with no linked constituent before allocation, leaving 986,729 retained rows. |
| `soft_credits.csv` | One soft credit; transaction table | Credit ID; Soft Credit Constituent ID → Constituent ID | 4,145 / 3,028 IDs (3,027 matched + SYN-ORPHAN) | FY2021–FY2026, 2020-07-01 to 2026-06-29 | Exact duplicates are removed first; valid-twin checks then remove invalid-recipient or nonpositive copies. Total removal: 192 rows; 3,953 remain. |
| `campaign_codes.csv` | One marketing/campaign code; reference table | Marketing Code; used by campaign members and payments | 29,249 / n.a. | No transaction date; includes initiative fields | No missing or duplicate keys or rows. All records are marked Active and Solicitation. |
| `campaign_members.csv` | One constituent solicitation/campaign-membership record; workflow/operational table | No unique key. constituent_id → Constituent ID; marketing_code → Marketing Code | 5,233,404 / 181,680 | FY2021–FY2026; campaign markers 2020-07-01 to 2025-07-01; responses through 2026-06-30 | Links are complete and valid. 56,689 exact duplicate rows; constituent/code pairs repeat in 58,786 rows, sometimes valid under the documented solicitation rules. |
| `passport_viewing.csv` | One constituent × fiscal year × genre viewing record; behavioral attribute table | Composite constituent_id + fiscal_year + genre; constituent ID → Constituent ID | 444,741 / 70,515 | FY2021–FY2026 | Composite key is unique; all IDs link; no duplicate rows; viewing counts are positive and watch percentages are within 0–1. |
| `cultivation.csv` | One constituent-year portfolio assignment; workflow/operational table | Composite synthetic_id + fiscal_year; IDs → Constituent ID and portfolio_id → officer portfolios | 4,000 / 2,398 | FY2022–FY2025 | Composite key is unique; all links and binary flags are valid; no duplicate rows. |
| `officer_portfolios.csv` | One officer portfolio; workflow/reference table | portfolio_id; referenced by cultivation | 8 / n.a. | Rollout FYs: 2023–2026 | No missing or duplicate keys or rows. |

**Key implications:** Payments, soft credits, campaign memberships, and Passport viewing are one-to-many relative to constituents and cannot be raw-joined without duplicating records. Campaign-member repeats are retained because they can represent valid solicitations. Content-based valid-twin checks remove copied Unite-payment and soft-credit rows, while unlinked legacy rows are removed before allocation. Individual giving uses non-organization direct payments plus soft credits, so organization-payment dollars are not double counted. Current constituent attributes are end-of-data snapshots and will need time-aware handling later to prevent leakage.

This structural check is designed to identify unexpected file sizes, schema
differences, exact duplicate records, and missing-data volume before detailed
quality checks begin. It does not make cleaning decisions or interpret any
findings.

### Missing-data checks

Missingness must be assessed by column because it can reflect unavailable
information, an unknown value, or a valid absence of activity.

```{r}
#| label: missing-data-checks

missing_data_summary <- imap_dfr(raw_data, function(data, file) {
  map_dfr(names(data), function(column) {
    values <- data[[column]]

    tibble(
      file_name = file,
      column_name = column,
      missing_na = sum(is.na(values)),
      percent_missing = 100 * mean(is.na(values)),
      blank_strings = if (is.character(values)) {
        sum(!is.na(values) & trimws(values) == "")
      } else {
        0L
      }
    )
  })
}) |>
  filter(missing_na > 0 | blank_strings > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(percent_missing))

knitr::kable(missing_data_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 1)
```

### Key and duplicate checks

Repeated activity is not always a duplicate: a donor can have many payments or
solicitations. Duplicates must therefore be evaluated using each dataset's
documented key.

```{r}
#| label: key-quality-checks

key_specs <- list(
  constituents = c("constituent_id"),
  unite_payments = c("payment_id"),
  campaign_codes = c("marketing_code"),
  passport_viewing = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year", "genre"),
  cultivation = c("synthetic_id", "fiscal_year"),
  officer_portfolios = c("portfolio_id")
)

key_quality_summary <- imap_dfr(key_specs, function(key_columns, dataset_name) {
  data <- get(dataset_name)
  missing_key <- reduce(map(key_columns, function(column) {
    values <- data[[column]]
    is.na(values) | (is.character(values) & trimws(values) == "")
  }), `|`)

  valid_keys <- data |>
    filter(!missing_key) |>
    select(all_of(key_columns))

  duplicate_key_rows <- valid_keys |>
    group_by(across(all_of(key_columns))) |>
    summarise(rows_per_key = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(rows_per_key > 1) |>
    summarise(rows_in_duplicated_keys = sum(rows_per_key)) |>
    pull(rows_in_duplicated_keys)

  tibble(
    dataset = dataset_name,
    total_rows = nrow(data),
    rows_with_missing_key = sum(missing_key),
    distinct_keys = nrow(distinct(valid_keys)),
    rows_in_duplicated_keys = replace_na(duplicate_key_rows, 0L)
  )
})

knitr::kable(key_quality_summary, format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
  exact_duplicate_rows = nrow(.x) - nrow(distinct(.x))
))

knitr::kable(exact_duplicate_summary, format = "pipe")
```

### Relationship and link checks

These checks verify whether foreign keys can be linked to their documented
parent tables before later aggregation. An unmatched ID does not automatically
mean an error because the synthetic data includes documented `SYN-ORPHAN` and
legacy-data exceptions.

```{r}
#| label: relationship-and-link-checks

relationship_specs <- tribble(
  ~child_dataset, ~child_key, ~parent_dataset, ~parent_key,
  "unite_payments", "donor_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "soft_credits", "soft_credit_constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "campaign_members", "constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "campaign_members", "marketing_code", "campaign_codes", "marketing_code",
  "unite_payments", "marketing_code", "campaign_codes", "marketing_code",
  "passport_viewing", "constituent_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "cultivation", "synthetic_id", "constituents", "constituent_id",
  "cultivation", "portfolio_id", "officer_portfolios", "portfolio_id"
)

relationship_quality_summary <- pmap_dfr(
  relationship_specs,
  function(child_dataset, child_key, parent_dataset, parent_key) {
    child_data <- get(child_dataset)
    parent_data <- get(parent_dataset)

    child_ids <- child_data |>
      transmute(foreign_key = as.character(.data[[child_key]]))
    parent_ids <- parent_data |>
      transmute(parent_key_value = as.character(.data[[parent_key]])) |>
      distinct()
    unmatched_ids <- child_ids |>
      anti_join(parent_ids, by = c("foreign_key" = "parent_key_value"))

    tibble(
      child_dataset_foreign_key = paste0(child_dataset, "$", child_key),
      parent_dataset_key = paste0(parent_dataset, "$", parent_key),
      total_child_rows = nrow(child_data),
      unmatched_child_rows = nrow(unmatched_ids),
      distinct_unmatched_ids = n_distinct(unmatched_ids$foreign_key)
    )
  }
)

knitr::kable(relationship_quality_summary, format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: legacy-payment-link-checks

legacy_constituent_columns <- paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7)
legacy_link_matrix <- legacy_payments |>

) > 0
legacy_ids <- legacy_link_matrix[

  rows_with_no_linked_constituent = sum(!legacy_has_link),
  percent_rows_with_no_linked_constituent = 100 * mean(!legacy_has_link),
  nonmissing_legacy_constituent_ids = length(legacy_ids),
  unmatched_legacy_constituent_ids = sum(!legacy_ids %in% constituent_ids)
)

knitr::kable(legacy_link_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 1)
```

### Value and date-range checks

These checks identify values outside plausible ranges and describe highly
skewed transaction amounts. An outlier is not automatically an error.

```{r}
#| label: transaction-amount-checks

amount_specs <- tribble(
  ~dataset, ~column,
  "unite_payments", "payment_amount",
  "legacy_payments", "payment_amount",
  "soft_credits", "credit_amount"
)

transaction_amount_summary <- pmap_dfr(amount_specs, function(dataset, column) {
  values <- get(dataset)[[column]]
  percentiles <- quantile(
    values,
    probs = c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )

  tibble(
    amount_field = paste0(dataset, "$", column),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    zero_values = sum(values == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    negative_values = sum(values < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum = min(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    percentile_25 = percentiles[1],
    median = percentiles[2],
    percentile_75 = percentiles[3],
    percentile_95 = percentiles[4],
    maximum = max(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})

knitr::kable(transaction_amount_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: range-and-validity-checks

summarise_range_validity <- function(values, field, lower_bound, upper_bound) {
  tibble(
    field = field,
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    minimum = min(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    count_below_lower_bound = sum(values < lower_bound, na.rm = TRUE),
    count_above_upper_bound = sum(values > upper_bound, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

range_validity_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarise_range_validity(constituents$age, "constituents$age", 0, 120),
  summarise_range_validity(passport_viewing$titles_viewed,
                           "passport_viewing$titles_viewed", 0, Inf),
  summarise_range_validity(passport_viewing$mean_percent_watched,
                           "passport_viewing$mean_percent_watched", 0, 1)
)

knitr::kable(range_validity_summary, format = "pipe", digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: date-range-checks

date_specs <- tribble(
  ~dataset, ~column,
  "unite_payments", "credit_date",
  "legacy_payments", "gift_date",
  "soft_credits", "credit_date",
  "campaign_members", "campaign_start_date",
  "campaign_members", "responded_date"
)

date_range_summary <- pmap_dfr(date_specs, function(dataset, column) {
  values <- as.Date(get(dataset)[[column]])
  nonmissing_dates <- values[!is.na(values)]

  tibble(
    date_field = paste0(dataset, "$", column),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(values)),
    minimum_date = if (length(nonmissing_dates) > 0) min(nonmissing_dates) else as.Date(NA),
    maximum_date = if (length(nonmissing_dates) > 0) max(nonmissing_dates) else as.Date(NA)
  )
})

knitr::kable(date_range_summary, format = "pipe")
```

### Summary of data quality findings
The raw tables contain 79 exact soft-credit duplicates and 56,689 exact campaign-member repeats. Campaign-member repeats are retained because a constituent can legitimately receive more than one solicitation. Soft-credit duplicates are removed as the first step of the completed valid-twin cleaning process.
Missingness is concentrated in fields that are either unavailable in this synthetic release or structurally blank. Several University degree/employment fields, legacy descriptive and premium fields, and campaign_description are entirely missing. Campaign response_type and responded_date are missing for most records because most solicitations did not receive a response. Spouse and marital-status fields are also largely incomplete, while only two age values are missing. The constituent table is an end-of-data snapshot, so its fields will require time-aware handling later to avoid using information that would not have been available at a historical prediction date.
Most foreign-key relationships are complete. The raw unmatched payment and soft-credit IDs use the documented SYN-ORPHAN placeholder, which is reported only as an audit check. Completed content-based valid-twin cleaning removes 36,044 Unite-payment copies and 192 soft-credit copies; the former includes 1,225 invalid campaign-code copies, while the latter includes 79 exact duplicates. It also removes 216,128 unlinked legacy rows before allocation. Amounts contain no negative values; nonpositive copies with valid twins are included in the verified removals, while large gifts are retained as plausible outliers. All checked dates and Passport viewing ranges were valid.


## 4. Cleaning decisions

The raw imported tables remain unchanged. The following rules will be applied
only when creating analysis-ready copies.

| Issue | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Unite payment copies | Remove only invalid donor-link, campaign-code-link, or nonpositive-amount rows when an otherwise identical valid twin exists. | Content-based twin checks avoid relying on synthetic ID labels. |
| Soft-credit copies | Remove exact duplicates first, then remove invalid-recipient or nonpositive-amount rows only when a valid twin exists. | Prevents duplicate credit while retaining unmatched records that lack a valid twin. |
| Unlinked legacy copies | Remove rows with no populated linked constituent ID before allocation. | They cannot be assigned to an individual donor. |
| Campaign-member rows | Retain all rows, including exact repeats. | Repeats can be valid solicitations. |
| Negative amounts | No action required. | None were found. |
| Fields that are 100% missing | Exclude from future feature creation. | They contain no information. |
| Structurally missing campaign response fields | Do not impute. | Missing `responded_date` and `response_type` generally indicate no recorded response. |
| Missing Passport records | Do not treat as zero viewing. | Preserve missingness and coverage as a separate concept. |
| Missing age and other partially missing constituent fields | Retain as missing for now. | Any model imputation must later be fit using training data only. |
| End-of-data constituent snapshot fields | Do not use directly as historical predictors unless a time-valid version can be created. | They could introduce data leakage. |
| Unite payments with an unmatched marketing code | Retain the payment for giving totals; treat campaign information as unknown unless the code can be mapped later. | The payment remains valid for giving analysis. |
| Large gifts | Retain. | They are plausible donor behavior, not demonstrated errors. |

The next subsection applies these rules to create analysis-ready copies while preserving the raw tables.

### Creating analysis-ready copies

The following code creates new analysis-ready objects while preserving all raw
objects for audit. These copies apply only the documented record-level rules;
they do not aggregate transactions, impute values, or create modeling features.

```{r}
#| label: create-analysis-ready-copies

content_twin_key <- function(data, columns) {
  do.call(
    paste,
    c(
      lapply(data[columns], function(value) replace_na(as.character(value), "<NA>")),
      sep = "\u001f"
    )
  )
}

valid_constituent_ids <- as.character(constituents$constituent_id)
valid_campaign_codes <- as.character(campaign_codes$marketing_code)

# A valid twin matches every substantive field except the record ID and the
# field that makes the candidate invalid. Synthetic labels are audit-only.
unite_payment_columns <- names(unite_payments)
unite_payment_candidates <- unite_payments |>
  mutate(
    valid_donor_link = donor_id %in% valid_constituent_ids,
    valid_campaign_link = marketing_code %in% valid_campaign_codes,
    valid_amount = coalesce(payment_amount > 0, FALSE)
  )

unite_donor_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "donor_id"))
)
unite_campaign_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "marketing_code"))
)
unite_amount_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  unite_payment_candidates,
  setdiff(unite_payment_columns, c("payment_id", "payment_amount"))
)

unite_payments_flagged <- unite_payment_candidates |>
  mutate(
    invalid_donor_copy = !valid_donor_link &
      unite_donor_twin_key %in% unite_donor_twin_key[valid_donor_link],
    invalid_campaign_copy = !valid_campaign_link &
      unite_campaign_twin_key %in% unite_campaign_twin_key[valid_campaign_link],
    nonpositive_amount_copy = !valid_amount &
      unite_amount_twin_key %in% unite_amount_twin_key[valid_amount],
    remove_valid_twin_copy = invalid_donor_copy | invalid_campaign_copy |
      nonpositive_amount_copy
  )

unite_payments_analysis <- unite_payments_flagged |>
  filter(!remove_valid_twin_copy) |>
  mutate(
    positive_amount = valid_amount,
    campaign_code_matched = valid_campaign_link
  )

soft_credit_exact_duplicate <- duplicated(soft_credits)
soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication <- soft_credits |>
  filter(!soft_credit_exact_duplicate)
soft_credit_columns <- names(soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication)
soft_credit_candidates <- soft_credits_after_exact_deduplication |>
  mutate(
    valid_recipient_link = soft_credit_constituent_id %in% valid_constituent_ids,
    valid_amount = coalesce(credit_amount > 0, FALSE)
  )

soft_recipient_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  soft_credit_candidates,
  setdiff(soft_credit_columns, c("credit_id", "soft_credit_constituent_id"))
)
soft_amount_twin_key <- content_twin_key(
  soft_credit_candidates,
  setdiff(soft_credit_columns, c("credit_id", "credit_amount"))
)

soft_credits_flagged <- soft_credit_candidates |>
  mutate(
    invalid_recipient_copy = !valid_recipient_link &
      soft_recipient_twin_key %in% soft_recipient_twin_key[valid_recipient_link],
    nonpositive_amount_copy = !valid_amount &
      soft_amount_twin_key %in% soft_amount_twin_key[valid_amount],
    remove_valid_twin_copy = invalid_recipient_copy | nonpositive_amount_copy,
    positive_amount = valid_amount
  )

soft_credits_analysis <- soft_credits_flagged |>
  filter(!remove_valid_twin_copy)

legacy_id_columns <- paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7)
legacy_payment_candidates <- legacy_payments |>
  mutate(
    has_linked_constituent = if_any(
      all_of(legacy_id_columns),
      ~ !is.na(.x) & trimws(as.character(.x)) != ""
    ),
    remove_unlinked_copy = !has_linked_constituent
  )
legacy_payments_analysis <- legacy_payment_candidates |>
  filter(!remove_unlinked_copy)

campaign_members_analysis <- campaign_members

organization_constituents <- constituents |>
  filter(
    primary_constituent_type == "Organization" |
      str_detect(
        coalesce(as.character(constituent_type), ""),
        regex("Organization", ignore_case = TRUE)
      )
  ) |>
  select(constituent_id, primary_constituent_type, constituent_type)

unite_payments_analysis <- unite_payments_analysis |>
  mutate(organization_payment = donor_id %in% organization_constituents$constituent_id)

constituents_analysis <- constituents
passport_viewing_analysis <- passport_viewing
cultivation_analysis <- cultivation
officer_portfolios_analysis <- officer_portfolios
campaign_codes_analysis <- campaign_codes
```

```{r}

  tibble(
    dataset = "unite_payments",
    raw_rows = nrow(unite_payments),
    exact_duplicates_removed = NA_integer_,
    invalid_donor_link_copies_removed = sum(
```
